level1.question: Magkano ang De Minimis Threshold na FOB o FCA value, kung saan walang duty o tax na kinokolekta sa imported goods, maliban kung ma-adjust sa ilalim ng Section 423 ng CMTA?
level1.reason: Sec. 3.16: ang De Minimis Threshold ay FOB o FCA value na hindi lalampas sa Php10,000.00, o as may be adjusted under Section 423 ng CMTA, kung saan walang duty o tax na kinokolekta.

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa goods of a commercial nature na may FOB o FCA value na Php50,000.00 o higit pa?

choices.A: Category 2
choices.B: Category 3
choices.D: Category 1 (Correspondence and Documents)

level1.reason: Sec. 3.23: ang High-Value Goods (Category 4) ay goods of a commercial nature na may FOB o FCA value na Php50,000.00 o over. Ang Category 3 ay mas mataas sa De Minimis Threshold pero mas mababa sa Php50,000.00.

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa Freight Forwarders at Customs Brokers na itinalaga ng digital platform providers para i-proseso ang clearance at release ng e-Commerce goods?

choices.A: Clearance Agent
choices.B: Value Added Service Provider
choices.D: Ultimate Consignee

level1.reason: Sec. 3.8: ang Clearance Agent ay tumutukoy sa Freight Forwarders at Customs Brokers na itinalaga ng digital platform providers para sa clearance at release ng e-Commerce goods.

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang oras mula sa pagdating ng carrying aircraft o vessel dapat isumite ang supplemental manifest para sa cargoes na hindi nakalista sa e-CIFCM?

choices.A: Dalawampu't apat (24) na oras
choices.B: Labindalawang (12) oras
choices.D: Anim (6) na oras

level1.reason: Sec. 7.3: ang cargoes na hindi nakalista sa e-CIFCM ay dapat saklawin ng supplemental manifest na isusumite within six (6) hours upon arrival ng carrying aircraft o vessel.

level1.question: Sino ang kinakailangang magbukas at magmantini ng Prepayment Account sa Bureau para ma-guarantee ang agarang bayad ng duties, taxes, at other charges sa e-Commerce Goods?

choices.A: Digital Platform Providers
choices.B: Freight Forwarders na accredited ng Bureau
choices.D: Ultimate Consignees

level1.reason: Section 12: ang Freight Forwarders na accredited ng Bureau para mag-proseso at mag-release ng e-Commerce Goods ang magbubukas at magmamantini ng Prepayment Accounts sa in-house bank/Cashier ng Bureau.

level1.question: Hanggang ilang porsiyento lamang ng Import Processing Fee na ipinapataw ng Bureau ang maaaring singilin ng EPS Service Provider bilang processing fee para sa cross-border e-Commerce goods?

choices.A: Limang porsiyento (5%)
choices.B: Dalawampung porsiyento (20%)
choices.D: Labinlimang porsiyento (15%)

level1.reason: Sec. 5.6: ang EPS Service Provider ay maaari lamang mag-charge ng processing fee na hindi lalampas sa sampung porsiyento (10%) ng Import Processing Fee na ipinataw ng Bureau para sa cross-border e-Commerce goods.

level1.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod ang hindi ipoproseso bilang e-Commerce goods ayon sa Section 10?

choices.A: Importations na classified bilang Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C) transactions
choices.B: Low-Value, Dutiable Goods (Category 3)
choices.D: Low-Value, Non-Dutiable Goods (Category 2)

level1.reason: Sec. 10.3: hindi ipoproseso bilang e-Commerce goods ang importations na classified sa ilalim ng Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C) transactions. Ayon sa Sec. 5.1, ang Category 2, 3, at 4 ay maaaring i-proseso sa e-Commerce Processing System.

level1.question: Gaano kadalas dapat i-review ang CAO 01-2025, maliban kung may ibang nakasaad?

choices.A: Bawat taon
choices.B: Bawat dalawang (2) taon
choices.D: Bawat tatlong (3) taon

level1.reason: Section 16: maliban kung may ibang nakasaad, ang CAO ay ire-review bawat tatlong (3) taon at aamyendahan o rerepasuhin kung kinakailangan. Ang Commissioner ay nagre-review ng fee structure ng EPS Service Providers kada taon (Sec. 5.8), na ibang provision.

level1.question: Sino lamang ang pinapayagang gumamit ng dedicated e-Commerce Processing System para sa clearance at release ng e-Commerce goods?

choices.A: Lahat ng importers
choices.B: Mga registered Customs Brokers lamang
choices.D: Digital Platform Providers lamang

level1.reason: Sec. 6.2: only accredited e-Commerce stakeholders ang pinapayagang gumamit ng dedicated e-Commerce Processing System. Ayon sa Sec. 6.1, kasama sa kailangang ma-accredit ang e-Commerce operators, digital platform providers, e-retailers, VASPs, freight forwarders, at brokers.

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa actual price o value ng isang goods for sale, sa Philippine currency, ayon sa posted sa digital platform sa petsa ng sale, hindi kasama ang transport at insurance costs maliban kung kasama na sa presyo?

choices.A: Intrinsic Value
choices.B: FOB Value
choices.D: De Minimis Threshold

level1.reason: Sec. 3.27: ang Intrinsic Value ay ang actual price o value ng goods for sale, sa Philippine currency, ayon sa posted sa digital platform sa date of sale, excluding transport at insurance costs, at iba pang taxes at charges, unless kasama na sa price at hindi hiwalay na nakasaad sa invoice.

level2.question: Lorna bought a pair of shoes from an e-marketplace. The FOB value is Php8,500.00, and the shipment is cleared through an accredited freight forwarder. Under CAO 01-2025, how is the shipment classified and what charge applies?

choices.A: Category 2; no duty or tax is collected, but an Import Processing Charge is imposed
choices.B: Category 3; duties and taxes are collected in addition to the Import Processing Charge
choices.C: Category 2; no duty, tax, or Import Processing Charge is collected on the shipment
choices.D: Category 1; the shipment is treated as correspondence and no charge is imposed

level2.reason: Under Sec. 3.29, goods with an FOB or FCA value not exceeding the De Minimis Threshold are Low-Value, Non-Dutiable Goods (Category 2), and Sec. 3.16 sets the threshold at Php10,000.00, below which no duty or tax is collected. Php8,500.00 does not exceed it. Section 9 provides that the Bureau shall impose import processing charges on e-Commerce goods within the De Minimis threshold, so the charge still applies.

level2.question: A freight forwarder is processing two e-Commerce parcels of a commercial nature. Parcel X has an FOB value of Php10,000.00, and Parcel Y has an FOB value of Php50,000.00. How are the parcels classified?

choices.A: Parcel X is Category 3, and Parcel Y is Category 3
choices.B: Parcel X is Category 2, and Parcel Y is Category 3
choices.C: Parcel X is Category 2, and Parcel Y is Category 4
choices.D: Parcel X is Category 3, and Parcel Y is Category 4

level2.reason: Under Sec. 3.29, Category 2 covers an FOB or FCA value not exceeding the De Minimis Threshold of Php10,000.00 (Sec. 3.16), so Parcel X at exactly Php10,000.00 is Category 2. Under Sec. 3.23, Category 4 covers an FOB or FCA value of Php50,000.00 or over, so Parcel Y at exactly Php50,000.00 is Category 4. Category 3 (Sec. 3.28) is only for values above the threshold but less than Php50,000.00.

level2.question: Ramon, a private individual abroad, sold his personal used camera to his friend Carla in Manila through a social media page. The sale was for personal purposes and was not made in the ordinary course of business. The camera was shipped to Carla. How will the Bureau treat the importation under CAO 01-2025?

choices.A: It is processed as Category 2 e-Commerce goods through the dedicated e-Commerce Processing System
choices.B: It is not processed as e-Commerce goods because it is a Consumer-to-Consumer transaction
choices.C: It is processed as Category 3 e-Commerce goods because it was sold through a social media platform
choices.D: It is not processed as e-Commerce goods because social media pages are not Digital Platforms

level2.reason: Sec. 3.11 defines a Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C) transaction as one between end-users for personal, family, or household purposes, not done in the ordinary course of business, regardless of the platform used. Sec. 10.3 excludes C2C importations from e-Commerce goods processing. Social media platforms are even listed as examples of Digital Platforms in Sec. 3.14, so option D is wrong.

level2.question: A freight forwarder declared a parcel of commercial goods as "without commercial value" on its documents. The parcel is not Correspondence and Documents (Category 1). What is the result under CAO 01-2025?

choices.A: The parcel is processed as Category 2 goods because its declared value is zero
choices.B: The parcel is processed as e-Commerce goods, with the Bureau fixing its value
choices.C: The parcel is processed as Category 1 goods exempt from any value declaration
choices.D: The parcel is excluded from e-Commerce processing, and the forwarder must declare its specific value with supporting documents, if any

level2.reason: Sec. 10.1 excludes importations declared as without commercial value, or of no commercial value, from e-Commerce goods processing. The freight forwarder, NVOCC, consolidator, or Clearance Agent must then declare the specific value of the goods, supported by an available invoice, receipt, or equivalent document. The only exception is Correspondence and Documents under Category 1, which the parcel is not.

level2.question: An aircraft carrying e-Commerce shipments arrived at 2:00 PM. After arrival, the freight forwarder found that one parcel was not listed in the e-CIFCM it had submitted. By what time must a supplemental manifest covering the parcel be submitted?

choices.A: 8:00 PM on the same day
choices.B: 2:00 PM on the following day
choices.D: 10:00 PM on the same day

level2.reason: Sec. 7.3 requires cargoes not listed in the e-CIFCM to be covered by a supplemental manifest submitted within six (6) hours upon arrival of the carrying aircraft or vessel. Six hours after 2:00 PM is 8:00 PM on the same day. Under Sec. 7.4, unmanifested goods are subject to fines and penalties under the CMTA.

level2.question: A misrouted e-Commerce shipment handled by an accredited freight forwarder arrived at a port. It was not re-exported within twenty-four (24) hours from arrival. Which of the following answers for the duties, taxes, and other charges that should have been collected?

choices.A: The Digital Platform Provider's data-sharing guarantee
choices.B: The ultimate consignee, as the buyer of the goods
choices.C: The freight forwarder's Prepayment Account with the Bureau
choices.D: The Value Added Service Provider's accreditation bond

level2.reason: Section 12 requires accredited Freight Forwarders to open and maintain Prepayment Accounts. The account also answers for the duties, taxes, and other charges that should have been collected when mis-sorted or misrouted shipments were not re-exported within twenty-four (24) hours from arrival, or when, having been exported, no proof of landing was presented.

level2.question: The Bureau imposed an Import Processing Fee of Php600.00 on a cross-border e-Commerce shipment cleared through an EPS Service Provider. The provider's fees collected from users of the System, at the published rate, totaled Php300,000.00. What is the maximum processing fee the provider may charge on that shipment, and what service fee does the Bureau collect from the provider?

choices.A: Php60.00 per shipment; Php3,000.00 service fee
choices.B: Php60.00 per shipment; Php30,000.00 service fee
choices.C: Php30.00 per shipment; Php30,000.00 service fee
choices.D: Php600.00 per shipment; Php30,000.00 service fee

level2.reason: Sec. 5.6 caps the EPS Service Provider's processing fee at ten percent (10%) of the Import Processing Fee, so 10% x Php600 = Php60.00. Sec. 5.7 provides that the Bureau collects from the provider a service fee for monitoring and supervision equivalent to ten percent (10%) of the fees collected, so 10% x Php300,000 = Php30,000.00.

level2.question: Delta Customs Brokerage, a customs broker designated by a digital platform provider as Clearance Agent for e-Commerce goods, has not been accredited with the Bureau for e-Commerce transactions. May it lodge e-Commerce goods declarations through the dedicated e-Commerce Processing System?

choices.A: Yes, because customs brokers are already licensed by the Professional Regulation Commission
choices.B: Yes, if the digital platform provider that designated it is accredited
choices.C: No, because only digital platform providers may use the system
choices.D: No, because only accredited e-Commerce stakeholders may use the system

level2.reason: Sec. 6.1 requires all e-Commerce stakeholders, including brokers and freight forwarders, to be accredited with the Bureau for e-Commerce transactions. Sec. 6.2 allows only accredited e-Commerce stakeholders to use the dedicated e-Commerce Processing System. A broker's PRC license (Sec. 3.13) or its principal's accreditation does not substitute for its own accreditation.

level2.question: An accredited platform ships two parcels to consumers in the Philippines. Parcel 1 contains goods classified as prohibited under the CMTA. Parcel 2 contains regulated goods that need a permit from a concerned regulatory agency. How does CAO 01-2025 treat the two parcels?

choices.A: Parcel 1 is not allowed even for e-Commerce purposes, while Parcel 2 is subject to the existing laws and regulations of the regulatory agency
choices.B: Both parcels are allowed because they were bought through an accredited platform and e-Commerce rules govern them
choices.C: Parcel 1 is allowed if its value is within the De Minimis Threshold, while Parcel 2 is not allowed at all
choices.D: Both parcels are not allowed because regulated goods are treated in the same way as prohibited goods

level2.reason: Section 11 provides that goods classified as prohibited under the CMTA and other laws shall not be allowed even for e-Commerce purposes. Regulated and restricted goods are subject to the existing laws and regulations of the concerned regulatory agencies, which is why Parcel 2 is not banned outright. Sec. 6.3.2 likewise bars the sale of regulated goods unless the necessary permits are submitted.

level2.question: A Bureau officer obtained shipment data that a digital platform provider had submitted to the Bureau and gave it to a private marketing firm for a fee. How does CAO 01-2025 treat this act?

choices.A: It is allowed because the data is already in the Bureau's possession
choices.B: It is covered only by a written reprimand under Section 13
choices.C: It is a violation, and the officer shall be proceeded against under Section 15
choices.D: It is allowed if the marketing firm agrees to keep the data confidential

level2.reason: Section 13 requires the Bureau to treat information from digital platform providers and e-retailers with utmost confidentiality and for official purposes only. Personnel who use it for other than official or legal purposes shall be proceeded against under Section 15, which provides penalties and sanctions as may be provided by law.

level1.question: Ayon sa amended Sec. 4.1, ano ang basehan ng singil na Php1,087.00 para sa Entrance and Clearance ng Vessel?

choices.A: Per day
choices.B: Per vessel
choices.D: Per container

level1.reason: Section 2 ng CAO 02-2025 (amending Sec. 4.1): Php1,087.00 ang Entrance and Clearance per vessel. Ang Loading and Unloading ay per day naman (Php4,500.00).

level1.question: Ano ang basehan ng pagbabayad ng Import Processing Charge para sa Cross-Border De Minimis Goods na personal o direktang pino-proseso ng claimant?

choices.A: Per ultimate consignee
choices.B: Per goods declaration
choices.D: Per container

level1.reason: Sec. 5.5.a (Section 4 ng CAO): ang bayad para sa personal na pino-proseso ng claimant ay per consignment note basis. Ang De Minimis Goods na cleared through a third party ay per ultimate consignee basis (Sec. 5.5.b).

level1.question: Magkano ang Import Processing Charge para sa De Minimis Goods na cleared through a third party, tulad ng Customs Broker o Freight Forwarder, kung ang FOB/FCA value ay mahigit Php2,000.00 hanggang Php10,000.00?

choices.A: 2.5% Ad Valorem
choices.D: 5% Ad Valorem

level1.reason: Sec. 5.5.b: 2.5% Ad Valorem ang rate para sa FOB/FCA value na mahigit Php2,000.00 hanggang Php10,000.00. Php50.00 naman ang rate kung hanggang Php2,000.00 lamang.

level1.question: Magkano ang AEO Application Charge ng isang Authorized Economic Operator na nasa Small na DTI-based category?

choices.D: Php0.00

level1.reason: Amended Sec. 5.12 (Section 5 ng CAO): Php0.00 ang application charge ng Micro at Small. Php5,000.00 ang Medium at Php10,000.00 ang Large.

level1.question: Magkano ang Legal Research Fund (LRF) na kinokolekta sa bawat document na inilalabas ng Bureau ayon sa amended Section 6?

choices.A: Php10.00 o 1% ng filing fee, alinman ang mas mababa
choices.B: Php10.00 o 1% ng filing fee, alinman ang mas mataas
choices.C: Php30.00 o 1% ng filing fee, alinman ang mas mataas
choices.D: Php10.00 o 5% ng filing fee, alinman ang mas mataas

level1.reason: Section 7 ng CAO 02-2025 (amending Section 6): ang LRF ay Php10.00 o 1% ng filing fee na ipinataw, whichever is higher. Ang CDS ay Php100.00 at ang DST ay Php30.00.

level1.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod ang hindi sakop ng Import Processing Charge ayon sa amended Sec. 5.5?

choices.A: De Minimis Goods na cleared through a Customs Broker
choices.B: Dutiable Shipments na filed under Consumption procedure
choices.C: De Minimis Goods na dala ng Travelers, accompanied man o unaccompanied baggage
choices.D: De Minimis Goods na personal na pino-proseso ng claimant na lampas Php5,000.00

level1.reason: Sec. 5.5.d: ang De Minimis Goods na dala ng Travelers, accompanied o unaccompanied baggage, ay hindi subject sa Import Processing Charge. Ang tatlo pang pagpipilian ay may kaukulang rate sa Sec. 5.5.a, 5.5.b, at 5.5.c.

level1.question: Magkano ang meal allowance per meal na babayaran kung ang travel time ng Customs officer ay sumasakop sa alinmang bahagi ng itinakdang oras ng breakfast, lunch, o supper?
level1.reason: Sec. 8.6.2: Php200.00 per meal ang meal allowance, at babayaran lamang kung ang travel time ay sumasakop sa anumang bahagi ng breakfast (6:00-8:00 AM), lunch (12:00 Noon-1:00 PM), o supper (6:00-8:00 PM).

level1.question: Kailan magsisimula ang pagpapataw ng Aircraft Supervision Fee na dinefer ng CAO 02-2025?

choices.A: January 1, 2025
choices.B: March 1, 2025

level1.reason: Section 9 ng CAO 02-2025: ang imposition ng Aircraft Supervision Fee (Section 4.2 ng CAO 02-2024) ay dinefer at magsisimula sa May 1, 2025.

level1.question: Hanggang kailan pansamantalang sinuspinde ang pagpapataw ng Certificate of Origin Processing Charge ayon sa Section 10?

choices.A: Hanggang magsimula ang Aircraft Supervision Fee sa May 1, 2025
choices.B: Hanggang matapos ang unang taon ng pagpapatupad ng CAO 02-2025
choices.C: Hanggang alisin ng Commissioner, na aprubado ng Secretary of Finance
choices.D: Hanggang mag-isyu ang Bureau ng bagong CMO tungkol dito

level1.reason: Section 10: temporarily suspended ang Certificate of Origin Processing Charge (Sec. 5.29 ng CAO 02-2024) until lifted by the Commissioner, as approved by the Secretary of Finance. Walang nakasaad na fixed na petsa.

level1.question: Anong Section ng CMTA ang binanggit bilang batayan ng special nature of operations ng Air Express Cargo Operators (AECO), kaya hindi sila sakop ng ilang fees?

choices.A: Section 439
choices.B: Section 1211
choices.D: Section 1301

level1.reason: Section 11: hindi sakop ang AECO sa Aircraft Supervision Fee, Underguarding Fee for Transfers, Off-Hours Fee, at CFW Fee dahil sa special nature ng operations nila ayon sa Section 439 ng CMTA.

level2.question: Cebu Star, a vessel engaged in foreign commerce, entered and cleared at a Port of Entry where Customs Services were rendered. Boarding formalities were conducted once. Entrance and clearance services were rendered over 2 days, and loading and unloading were supervised for 3 days. No bunkering or emergency services were requested. Under the amended Section 4.1, what total Vessel Supervision Fee is due?
level2.reason: Under amended Sec. 4.1, boarding formalities cost Php2,250.00 per vessel, entrance and clearance cost Php1,087.00 per vessel (not per day), and loading and unloading cost Php4,500.00 per day. The computation is Php2,250 + Php1,087 + (3 x Php4,500 = Php13,500) = Php16,837.00. The 2 days of entrance and clearance services do not multiply the fee.

level2.question: A customs broker cleared two de minimis consignments under a Special Power of Attorney for two different ultimate consignees. The goods of the first consignee have an FOB value of Php1,800.00, and those of the second have an FOB value of Php8,000.00. Under Section 5.5.b, what total Import Processing Charge is due?
level2.reason: Sec. 5.5.b applies to de minimis goods cleared through a third party and is charged per ultimate consignee. The first consignee (up to Php2,000.00) pays Php50.00. The second (above Php2,000.00 up to Php10,000.00) pays 2.5% ad valorem, or 2.5% x Php8,000 = Php200.00. The total is Php50 + Php200 = Php250.00.

level2.question: Juan personally processed, as claimant, two separate cross-border de minimis consignment notes. The first has an FOB value of Php4,800.00, and the second has an FOB value of Php9,500.00. What total Import Processing Charge must he pay?

choices.A: Php0.00

level2.reason: Sec. 5.5.a charges personally processed de minimis goods per consignment note. A value of Php5,000.00 and below pays Php0.00, while a value above Php5,000.00 but not more than Php10,000.00 pays Php125.00. The first note pays nothing and the second pays Php125.00, for a total of Php125.00. The 2.5% ad valorem rate applies only to goods cleared through a third party.

level2.question: An importer filed a goods declaration under the Consumption clearance procedure for goods with a dutiable value of Php620,000.00. The FOB value of the goods is above Php10,000.00. Excluding the LRF, what total Import Processing Charge, CDS, and DST must be paid for this declaration?
level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.5.c, a dutiable value above Php500,000.00 up to Php750,000.00 pays Php1,500.00, in addition to the CDS of Php100.00 and the BIR DST of Php30.00. The total is Php1,500 + Php100 + Php30 = Php1,630.00.

level2.question: Customs Officer Reyes used his own private vehicle to travel from his permanent official station to a port of assignment to render Customs Services. He now claims reimbursement for the cost of gasoline. How will his claim be treated?

choices.A: Gasoline is reimbursed in full because it is a transportation expense of the trip
choices.B: He may not claim gasoline but may claim the equivalent cost of customary transportation
choices.C: He may not claim any transportation reimbursement because a private vehicle was used for the trip
choices.D: Gasoline is reimbursed only up to the cost of the customary mode of transportation

level2.reason: Sec. 8.2 states that if a private vehicle is used, no reimbursement of the cost of gasoline and fuel is allowed. The official is, however, entitled to the equivalent cost of the customary mode of transportation.

level2.question: A Customs officer's transportation and daily travel expenses are furnished by a shipping line for an assignment. The officer leaves the official station at 11:00 AM and arrives at the vessel boarding point at 7:30 PM. Under Section 8.6.2, what total meal allowance is payable?
level2.reason: Sec. 8.6.2 pays Php200.00 per meal only if the travel time embraces any part of breakfast (6:00-8:00 AM), lunch (12:00 Noon-1:00 PM), or supper (6:00-8:00 PM). Travel from 11:00 AM to 7:30 PM covers lunch and part of supper, but not breakfast. That is 2 meals x Php200 = Php400.00.

level2.question: A Customs officer is assigned to a vessel at a pier 40 km from the Customs station, and the shipping line is the requesting party. Under Section 8.6.3, how much land transportation allowance is payable for traveling to the pier and back?
level2.reason: Sec. 8.6.3 provides for a land transportation allowance of Php25.00 per km from the Customs station to its destination, and vice-versa, payable by the shipping line or requesting party. The round trip is 40 km x 2 = 80 km, and 80 x Php25 = Php2,000.00.

level2.question: A Customs officer paid his own daily travel expenses and travel expenses in advance for an assignment to a vessel. The shipping line has already reimbursed him for the same expenses. May he still claim reimbursement from the Bureau?

choices.A: Yes, because the Bureau must pay these expenses regardless of the source
choices.B: Yes, but only for the transportation expenses
choices.C: Yes, if he returns the shipping line's reimbursement to the Bureau
choices.D: No, because he can no longer claim reimbursement from the Bureau

level2.reason: Sec. 8.6.5 provides that when the DTE and travel expenses were paid in advance by the Customs officer and already reimbursed by the shipping line, the officer can no longer claim reimbursement from the Bureau. This prevents double payment (see also Sec. 8.5).

level2.question: An Air Express Cargo Operator (AECO) transferred express shipments from a discharging aircraft to an Off-Terminal CFW covered by a Transfer Note. Will the Php500.00 per Transfer Note Underguarding Fee for Transfers be imposed on the AECO?

choices.A: Yes, Php500.00 per Transfer Note applies to every party that transfers goods
choices.B: Yes, but only when the AECO transfers goods to a CBW
choices.C: No, because AECOs are not subject to the Underguarding Fee for Transfers
choices.D: No, because the fee is payable only by Customs Brokers

level2.reason: Section 11 provides that AECOs are not subject to the Aircraft Supervision Fee, Underguarding Fee for Transfers (Sec. 4.5), Off-Hours Fee, and CFW Fee, due to the special nature of their operations under Section 439 of the CMTA. Their supervision fee is governed by CAO No. 5-2020 as implemented by CMO No. 9-2021.

level2.question: Pacific Air, a regular airline and not an AECO, had one aircraft engaged in foreign commerce land and depart at an international airport on April 25, 2025, and another aircraft do the same on May 6, 2025. Customs Services were rendered for both. For which aircraft may the Aircraft Supervision Fee be imposed?

choices.A: Only the aircraft that landed and departed on May 6, 2025
choices.B: Only the aircraft that landed and departed on April 25, 2025
choices.D: Neither aircraft, because the fee is suspended until lifted by the Commissioner

level2.reason: Section 9 states that the imposition of the Aircraft Supervision Fee is deferred and shall commence on May 1, 2025. Only the May 6, 2025 aircraft falls on or after that date. The suspension until lifted by the Commissioner in Section 10 applies to the Certificate of Origin Processing Charge, not to this fee.

level1.question: Saang pondo mapupunta ang mga Customs Service Fee sa Section 4, na maaaring gamitin sa allowances at overtime services ng Customs personnel?

choices.A: General Fund
choices.B: Trust Fund
choices.D: Regulatory Fund

level1.reason: Sec. 4: ang mga Fees sa Section 4 ay kokolektahin at mapupunta sa Trust Fund na maaaring gamitin sa allowances at overtime services. Ang Dues and Charges sa Section 5 naman ay mapupunta sa General Fund.

level1.question: Magkano ang Aircraft Supervision Fee na binabayaran ng Airline o ng agent nito para sa bawat Aircraft na engaged in foreign commerce na lumapag at umalis sa international airport of entry?
level1.reason: Sec. 4.2: Php4,500.00 ang Aircraft Supervision Fee para sa bawat Aircraft na engaged in foreign commerce na lumapag at umalis sa international airport of entry kung saan may Customs Services na ibinigay.

level1.question: Magkano ang AEO Annual Supervision Fee ng isang Authorized Economic Operator na nasa Small na DTI-based category?

choices.D: Php0.00

level1.reason: Sec. 4.4: Php9,000.00 ang fee ng Small (total assets na Php3,000,001.00 hanggang Php15,000,000.00). Php0.00 ang Micro, Php24,000.00 ang Medium, at Php36,000.00 ang Large.

level1.question: Magkano ang Customs Documentary Stamp (CDS), Documentary Stamp Tax (DST), at Legal Research Fee (LRF) na kinokolekta sa bawat document na inilalabas ng Bureau?

choices.A: CDS Php30.00, DST Php100.00, LRF Php10.00
choices.B: CDS Php100.00, DST Php10.00, LRF Php30.00

level1.question: Magkano ang Export Processing Charge para sa CDS at BIR DST na binabayaran ng Exporter sa bawat Export Declaration, maliban kung exempted sa ilalim ng umiiral na batas?

level1.question: Magkano ang processing charge para sa Cross Border E-Commerce Goods na personal o direktang pino-proseso ng claimant, kung ang FOB/FCA value ng goods ay Php5,000.00 pababa?

choices.A: Free

level1.reason: Sec. 5.5.c: libre ang processing ng Cross Border E-Commerce Goods na personal o direktang pino-proseso ng claimant kung ang FOB/FCA value ay Php5,000.00 pababa. Php150.00 ang rate kung mahigit Php5,000.00 hanggang Php10,000.00.

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa trabahong ginagawa ng customs personnel sa labas ng kanyang Official Work Station, o sa overtime work para sa benepisyo ng concerned stakeholders, tulad ng boarding formalities sa Vessels at Aircrafts?

choices.A: Customs Facilities and Warehouses
choices.B: Third Party Service Provider
choices.D: Official Work Station

level1.reason: Sec. 3.9: ang Customs Services ay trabahong ginagawa ng customs personnel sa labas ng Official Work Station o ang Overtime Work para sa benepisyo ng concerned stakeholders. Ayon sa Sec. 3.19, ang Official Work Station ay ang lugar kung saan regular na nagtatrabaho ang empleyado.

level2.question: Pacific Dawn, a vessel engaged in foreign commerce, entered and cleared at a Port of Entry where Customs Services were rendered. The Bureau conducted boarding formalities once, rendered entrance and clearance services for 2 days, and supervised loading and unloading for 3 days. No bunkering or emergency services were requested. What total Vessel Supervision Fee is due?
level2.reason: Under Sec. 4.1, the fees are Php2,250.00 for boarding formalities per vessel, Php1,087.00 for entrance and clearance per day, and Php4,500.00 for loading and unloading per day. The computation is Php2,250 + (2 x Php1,087 = Php2,174) + (3 x Php4,500 = Php13,500) = Php17,924.00. The shipping line or its agent pays this fee.

level2.question: Kiwi Exports Co. filed an application for tax credit and refund of Php380,000.00, and the Bureau issued a Tax Credit Certificate (TCC) for the claim. Excluding CDS, DST, and LRF, what total Refund Processing Charge and TCC charge must Kiwi pay?
level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.7, a claim over Php300,000.00 to Php400,000.00 pays a Refund Processing Charge of Php1,500.00. Sec. 5.30 adds Php300.00 for every TCC issued, outside of the refund processing charge. The total is Php1,500 + Php300 = Php1,800.00.

level2.question: The District Collector issued a decision on a protest case filed by Lumen Imports Corp., involving duties and taxes of Php450,000.00. Lumen wishes to appeal the decision. Excluding CDS, DST, and LRF, what appeal fee must it pay?
level2.reason: Sec. 5.8(a) sets the appeal fee for decisions of the District Collector on protest cases according to the amount of duties and taxes. Over Php400,000.00 to Php500,000.00 is Php3,500.00. The flat Php5,000.00 in Sec. 5.8(b) applies only to decisions not related to seizure, abandonment, protest, or dispute settlement cases.

level2.question: Ana bought goods online with an FOB value of Php6,500.00, and her shipment was cleared through a consolidator. Ben bought goods online with the same FOB value and processed the clearance personally as claimant. Under Section 5.5, what is the combined Import Processing Charge for both shipments, excluding CDS, DST, and LRF?
level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.5.b, goods cleared through a consolidator or freight forwarder with an FOB/FCA value above Php5,000.00 but not more than Php7,000.00 pay Php300.00 (Ana). Under Sec. 5.5.c, goods processed personally by the claimant above Php5,000.00 but not more than Php10,000.00 pay Php150.00 (Ben). The combined charge is Php300 + Php150 = Php450.00.

level2.question: Bayanihan Logistics, classified as Medium under the DTI-based category with total assets of Php60,000,000.00, applied for accreditation as an Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) and was accredited. What AEO Application Charge and AEO Annual Supervision Fee apply to it?

choices.A: Php2,500.00 application charge and Php9,000.00 annual supervision fee
choices.B: Php5,000.00 application charge and Php24,000.00 annual supervision fee
choices.C: Php10,000.00 application charge and Php36,000.00 annual supervision fee
choices.D: Php5,000.00 application charge and Php9,000.00 annual supervision fee

level2.reason: Sec. 5.12 sets the AEO Application Charge for a Medium AEO at Php5,000.00. Sec. 4.4 sets the AEO Annual Supervision Fee for a Medium AEO (total assets above Php15,000,000.00 up to Php100,000,000.00) at Php24,000.00. Php60,000,000.00 falls within the Medium range.

level2.question: Orion Imports has previously paid charges for two cancellations or modifications of its goods declarations. It must now cancel a third goods declaration, and the Bureau confirms that the reason for the cancellation is a system error. What charge applies to this cancellation?

choices.A: Php1,000.00, charged as a first offense
choices.B: Php3,000.00, charged as a second offense
choices.C: Php5,000.00, as a third offense or more
choices.D: No charge, as it is due to a system error

level2.reason: Sec. 5.14 imposes Php1,000.00, Php3,000.00, and Php5,000.00 for the first, second, and third or more offense of cancellation or modification of a goods declaration, except when the reason for cancellation is a system error. Because the cancellation is due to a system error, no charge applies despite Orion's earlier cancellations.

level2.question: Pioneer Common Bonded Warehouse is a CCBW with three accredited members. Their total assets (excluding real estate) are Php2,500,000.00, Php12,000,000.00, and Php80,000,000.00. The operator has one extension warehouse, and one of the members also has one extension warehouse. What total annual supervision charge must be paid?
level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.31.3, the CCBW operator pays Php250,000.00. Members pay according to total assets: Php2.5 million is exempted, Php12 million (above Php3 million to Php15 million) pays Php25,000.00, and Php80 million (above Php50 million) pays Php100,000.00. Each extension warehouse of the operator or an accredited member pays Php50,000.00, so two extensions add Php100,000.00. The total is Php250,000 + Php0 + Php25,000 + Php100,000 + Php100,000 = Php475,000.00.

level2.question: Skyline Air will operate a chartered flight that will arrive in Manila and later depart from Manila. Its ground handler received the notice of the intended flight covering both the arrival and the departure. Under the Special Flight Supervision Fee, how much must be paid in total, and when?

choices.A: USD 350 in total, paid upon receipt of the flight notice
choices.B: USD 175 in total, paid upon landing of the aircraft in Manila
choices.C: USD 350 in total, paid after the flight departs from Manila
choices.D: USD 175 in total, because only the arrival is chargeable

level2.reason: Sec. 4.7 imposes USD 175 for every arrival or departure of chartered or special flights, to be paid by the ground handler or airline representative upon receipt of the notice of the intended flight. One arrival and one departure make two chargeable events, so the total is 2 x USD 175 = USD 350.

level2.question: Meridian Steel is an accredited Super Green Lane (SGL) importer. It lodged two goods declarations through the SGL facility, with FOB values of USD 150,000.00 and USD 250,000.00, and was issued one List of Importables (LOI). Excluding CDS, DST, and LRF, what total SGL Service Charge and LOI Processing Fee must it pay?
level2.reason: Sec. 5.33 charges Php2,500.00 per goods declaration with an FOB value of USD 200,000.00 and below (the USD 150,000 declaration) and Php3,000.00 for an FOB value above USD 200,000.00 (the USD 250,000 declaration). Sec. 4.9 charges Php1,000.00 for every LOI issued to an SGL accredited company. The total is Php2,500 + Php3,000 + Php1,000 = Php6,500.00.

level2.question: Zone Logistics Inc., a Free Zone Locator, requested underguarding services for 3 containers moving from a seaport to a Free Zone 18 km away, and for 2 containers moving from a Free Zone to the Port of Loading for export 45 km away. No E-TRACC, GTSB, or other means of physically securing the goods were availed of or required. What total Free Zone Locator Supervision Fee is due?
level2.reason: Under Sec. 4.3, movement from a seaport to a Free Zone pays Php500.00 per container if not exceeding 30 km, and movement from a Free Zone to the Port of Loading pays Php1,000.00 per container if exceeding 30 km. The computation is (3 x Php500 = Php1,500) + (2 x Php1,000 = Php2,000) = Php3,500.00. The fee would not apply only if other physical security means were availed of or required.

level1.question: Gaano katagal ang bisa ng Authority to Operate a CBW, na binibilang mula sa date ng approval ng application for establishment?

choices.B: Tatlong (3) taon
choices.D: Isang (1) taon

level1.question: Ilan ang pinapayagang bilang ng members ng isang Customs Common Bonded Warehouse (CCBW)?

choices.A: Hindi bababa sa lima (5) at hindi hihigit sa limampu (50)

level1.question: Anong dokumento ang inilalabas ng District Collector na nagpapahintulot sa transfer o sale ng imported raw materials, semi-finished products, o finished products sa ibang CBW, Client-Exporter, Client/End-User, o Free Zone locator para sa subsequent export?

level1.question: Sa isang MCBW, hanggang ilang porsiyento ng volume ng raw materials na entered for warehousing ang maaaring entered for consumption?

choices.A: Sampung porsiyento (10%)

choices.D: Limampung porsiyento (50%)

level1.question: Sino ang namumuno sa Customs Bonded Warehouse Committee (CBWC)?

choices.D: Assistant Commissioner ng PCAG

level1.question: Saan dapat i-file ang application para sa Authority to Operate a CBW, kasama ang application para maging member, subcontractor, Client-Exporter, o Client/End-User ng existing warehouse?

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang araw dapat kumilos ang Commissioner sa application para sa Authority to Operate mula nang matanggap ang recommendation ng CBWC?

choices.B: Dalawampung (20) calendar days
choices.D: Tatlumpung (30) working days

level1.question: Alin ang tamang katangian ng Authority to Operate a CBW ayon sa CAO?

choices.D: Maaaring ilipat sa bagong may-ari kapag naibenta ang CBW

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa paglabag kung saan ang imported material na pumasok sa warehousing scheme at papunta sa isang CBW, Free Zone locator/enterprise, o mula sa CBW papunta sa port o airport para sa exportation ay dinala sa ibang lugar na hindi nito intended destination?

choices.D: Transit

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa formula of conversion na inilalabas ng Industrial Technology Development Institute (ITDI) sa CBW operator at members para matukoy ang raw material usage at wastages ng isang finished product para sa export at liquidation?

choices.B: Wastage Valuation Data Base (WVDB)
choices.D: Statement of Monthly Raw Materials Importation Requirements (SMRMIR)

level2.question: Tahanan Common Bonded Warehouse is a Customs Common Bonded Warehouse with twelve (12) accredited members and one (1) extension warehouse. Using the schedule of annual supervision fees, how much total annual supervision fee must it pay?
level2.reason: Sec. 14.3 sets the annual supervision fee for a CCBW at Php250,000.00, plus Php100,000.00 for every member and Php50,000.00 for every extension warehouse. The computation is Php250,000 + (12 x Php100,000 = Php1,200,000) + Php50,000 = Php1,500,000.00.

level2.question: Cebu Garments Inc., a CBW operator, had two warehousing entries whose storage periods expired. Before the storage periods lapsed, it requested to export the finished goods late. The finished goods from Entry 1 were exported 12 days after the storage period expired, and those from Entry 2 were exported 36 days after. What total penalty for late exportation applies?
level2.reason: Sec. 15.7 imposes Php10,000.00 per entry for exportation 1-30 days after expiration of the storage period, and Php20,000.00 per entry for 31-45 days. Entry 1 (12 days) is Php10,000 and Entry 2 (36 days) is Php20,000, for a total of Php30,000.00. Sec. 8.11.3 allows late exportation when requested before the storage period lapses, subject to the applicable penalties.

level2.question: Mabini Plastics, a CBW operator, withdrew bonded resin from its warehouse without a duly processed withdrawal slip. This is its second offense, and no fraud is involved. The duties and taxes due on the withdrawn goods are Php800,000.00, all unpaid. What is its total monetary liability and other sanction under Section 15?

choices.A: Php1,200,000.00, plus suspension of warehousing privileges for six (6) months
choices.B: Php1,200,000.00, plus closure of the CBW as the second-offense penalty
choices.C: Php800,000.00, plus suspension of warehousing privileges for six (6) months
choices.D: Php1,600,000.00, plus closure of the CBW as the second-offense penalty

level2.reason: Withdrawal without a duly processed withdrawal slip is an unauthorized withdrawal (Sec. 3.49). Sec. 15.2.2 provides for the duties and taxes due plus a surcharge of fifty percent (50%) and suspension of warehousing privileges for six (6) months for a second offense. The computation is Php800,000 + (50% x Php800,000 = Php400,000) = Php1,200,000. Closure applies only to a third offense or one attended with fraud.

level2.question: Delta Foods obtained an Authority to Operate a CBW. The lease contract it submitted during the application had a term of only two (2) years, so the Authority was made co-terminus with that lease. Later, Delta Foods submitted a new lease contract with a ten (10)-year term. What is the validity of its Authority to Operate after the new lease is submitted?

choices.A: Three (3) years counted from the date the new lease contract is submitted
choices.B: Three (3) years counted from the original issuance date
choices.C: Ten (10) years, matching the term of the new lease contract
choices.D: It remains co-terminus with the original two (2)-year lease contract

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.3, if the submitted lease is shorter than three (3) years, the Authority is co-terminus with the lease unless a new Contract of Lease with a longer period is submitted. In that case, the Authority is amended to its maximum period of three (3) years counted from its date of original issuance, not from the new lease.

level2.question: Unity Common Bonded Warehouse already has thirty (30) accredited members. Kapitan Garments, whose projected duties and taxes for bonded goods importations are Php120,000,000.00 for one (1) year, applies to become a member. May the CCBW accept it as a member?

choices.A: No, because admitting it would bring the membership above the thirty (30)-member maximum
choices.B: Yes, because its projected duties and taxes do not exceed Php300,000,000.00
choices.C: No, because projected duties and taxes must be at least Php300,000,000.00 to qualify
choices.D: Yes, because the thirty (30)-member maximum applies only when a CCBW is first established

level2.reason: Sec. 6.1 allows a company to apply as a member if its projected duties and taxes do not exceed Php300,000,000.00 per year, which Kapitan Garments satisfies. However, Sec. 6.2 limits a CCBW to at least three (3) but not more than thirty (30) members. With thirty (30) members already, admitting another would exceed the maximum.

level2.question: The Commissioner denied the application of Sampaguita Textiles Corp. to renew its Authority to Operate a CBW. Sampaguita received the Notice of Denial and believes the grounds are unfounded. What may it do?

choices.A: Request reconsideration from the District Collector once the lacking documents are completed
choices.B: File a Motion for Reconsideration with the Commissioner within ten (10) days from receipt
choices.C: File a new application right away, since a denial by the Commissioner is final
choices.D: File a Motion for Reconsideration with the Commissioner within fifteen (15) days from receipt

level2.reason: Sec. 7.1 allows an applicant whose application to establish or renew was denied by the Commissioner to file a Motion for Reconsideration with the Commissioner within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the Notice of Denial, copy furnished the CBWC and the District Collector, stating the grounds for approval. The Commissioner then resolves it within twenty (20) days (Sec. 7.2).

level2.question: Pearl Electronics operates an MCBW whose main warehouse is under the District Collector of the Port of Cebu. It wants an extension warehouse located within the territorial jurisdiction of the District Collector of the Port of Davao. How will the application be treated?

choices.A: As an application for extension filed with the Cebu District Collector, who will coordinate with the Davao District Collector
choices.B: As an amendment of the Certificate of Authority to Operate filed with the Commissioner
choices.C: As a new application filed with the Davao District Collector, supported by the Section 5.1.2 documents
choices.D: As an application for relocation approved by the Cebu District Collector

level2.reason: Sec. 5.6.1 requires an extension warehouse to be within the territorial jurisdiction of the District Collector controlling the main warehouse. Under Sec. 5.6.4, an extension warehouse located outside that jurisdiction is treated as a new application filed with the District Collector having jurisdiction over the new site, supported by the same documents as in Sec. 5.1.2.

level2.question: Mango Nectar Inc., a CBW operator, received bonded flavorings, which are perishable goods, on March 1. Before the initial storage period ended, it submitted a written request for extension citing valid reasons, and the request was granted. Without express abandonment, what is the longest storage period from arrival before the goods are deemed abandoned?

choices.A: One (1) year from arrival
choices.B: Three (3) months from arrival
choices.D: Six (6) months from arrival

level2.reason: Sec. 3.39 includes flavorings among perishable goods. Under Sec. 8.11.2, the storage period for perishable goods is three (3) months from arrival, extendible for valid reasons upon written request for another three (3) months, for a total of six (6) months. Goods not withdrawn after the period are deemed abandoned unless expressly abandoned earlier.

level2.question: A fire destroyed imported fabrics stored in the bonded warehouse of Rizal Garments, a CBW operator, while the fabrics awaited production. The investigation found that the fire resulted from the operator's gross negligence in maintaining its electrical wiring. Who bears the duties and other charges on the destroyed goods?

choices.A: Rizal Garments, which must indemnify the Bureau for the duties and charges
choices.B: The Bureau, because CBWs are considered extensions of the customs premises
choices.C: The District Collector, because CBWs are under his supervision and control
choices.D: The Bureau and Rizal Garments, shared equally between them

level2.reason: Sec. 9.4 requires the CBW operator to indemnify the Bureau for the duties and other charges on goods lost or destroyed in storage due to the operator's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The same Section and Sec. 4.2 state that the government assumes no responsibility for the safekeeping of goods stored in a CBW.

level2.question: A member of a Customs Common Bonded Warehouse withdrew bonded goods without a duly processed requisition slip. The Bureau seeks to hold the CCBW operator responsible, but the operator argues that only the member should answer because the operator took no part in the violation. How should this be resolved under CAO 01-2022?

choices.A: The operator is not liable, because members are separate accredited entities
choices.B: The operator is liable only if the Bureau proves its gross negligence
choices.C: The operator is jointly and severally liable with its accredited member
choices.D: The operator is liable for half of the penalty, and the member for the other half

level2.reason: Sec. 10 provides that the CBW operator is jointly and severally liable with its accredited member and/or subcontractor for any violation committed. The operator's non-participation is not a defense, and the gross negligence standard in Sec. 9.4 applies only to indemnity for lost or damaged goods.

level1.question: Gaano katagal ang bisa (validity) ng customs accreditation ng Importer, maliban kung ito ay ma-suspend, ma-revoke, o ma-cancel?

choices.A: Isang (1) taon mula sa petsa ng pag-file ng application
choices.B: Isang (1) taon mula sa petsa ng approval
choices.C: Dalawang (2) taon mula sa petsa ng approval
choices.D: Tatlong (3) taon mula sa petsa ng approval

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 4.2, valid ang accreditation ng isang (1) taon mula sa date ng approval nito, unless suspended, revoked o cancelled. Hindi ito nagsisimula sa pag-file ng application.

level1.question: Magkano ang Processing Fee na kailangang bayaran para sa new application o renewal ng accreditation?

choices.A: Php1,000.00 para sa new application at renewal
choices.B: Php5,000.00 para sa new application at renewal
choices.C: Php2,000.00 para sa new application lamang; walang bayad ang renewal
choices.D: Php2,000.00 para sa new application at renewal

level1.reason: Sec. 4.5: Php2,000.00 ang Processing Fee para sa new application OR renewal ng accreditation, kaya parehong may bayad. Ang Php1,000.00 ay ang appeal fee, hindi ang Processing Fee.

level1.question: Ilang Importer lamang ang maaaring pagsilbihan ng isang Declarant of the Importer na hindi registered at licensed customs broker?

choices.A: Isang (1) Importer lamang
choices.B: Dalawang (2) Importers
choices.D: Walang limit, basta registered siya sa CPRS

level1.reason: Sec. 4.6, ikalawang talata: ang Declarant na hindi registered at licensed customs broker ay dapat naka-register sa CPRS at authorized na kumilos para sa isang Importer lamang.

level1.question: Ano ang tawag sa taong, kapalit ng compensation, ay nagsisilbing middleman sa pagbili at pagbebenta ng goods sa pagitan ng foreign supplier at local purchaser?

choices.A: Declarant of the Importer
choices.B: Responsible Officer
choices.D: Non-regular Importer

level1.reason: Sec. 3.6: ang Indentor ay ang taong, para sa compensation, ay middleman sa purchase and sale ng goods ng foreign supplier at local purchaser, at kapareho ng klase ng commercial broker o commission merchant.

level1.question: Ang Non-regular Importer ay nakikipag-transact sa Bureau nang isang beses lamang, saklaw ng iisang bill of lading o air waybill, sa loob ng ilang araw mula sa approval ng application for registration bilang non-regular importer?

choices.A: 180 araw
choices.B: 365 araw
choices.D: 30 araw

level1.reason: Sec. 3.9: ang Non-regular Importer ay ang nag-i-import at nakikipag-transact sa Bureau nang isang beses lamang, sa iisang bill of lading o air waybill, within 365 days mula sa approval ng registration.

level1.question: Gaano kaaga pinakamaaga maaaring mag-file ang Importer ng renewal application with complete supporting documents bago mag-expire ang accreditation?

choices.A: Hindi mas maaga sa tatlumpung (30) calendar days bago ang expiration
choices.B: Hindi mas maaga sa animnapung (60) calendar days bago ang expiration
choices.C: Hindi mas maaga sa labinlimang (15) calendar days bago ang expiration
choices.D: Hindi mas maaga sa pitong (7) working days bago ang expiration

level1.reason: Sec. 6.3: puwedeng mag-file ng renewal not earlier than thirty (30) calendar days prior to expiration. Ang pag-file na mas mababa sa pitong (7) working days bago mag-expire ay late renewal na, kaya hindi iyon ang pinakamaagang petsa.

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang araw dapat kumilos (acted upon) ang Bureau sa isang application mula nang matanggap ang complete documentary requirements?

choices.A: Pitong (7) calendar days
choices.B: Sampung (10) working days
choices.D: Pitong (7) working days

level1.reason: Sec. 7.3: dapat acted upon ang application within seven (7) working days from receipt of complete documentary requirements. Ang pitong (7) calendar days sa parehong Section ay para sa applicant na sasagot sa notice ng discrepancy.

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang araw mula nang mangyari ang pagbabago sa business information dapat i-report at isumite ng Importer ang kaugnay na dokumento sa Bureau?

choices.A: Pitong (7) working days
choices.B: Labinlimang (15) calendar days
choices.D: Tatlumpung (30) calendar days

level1.reason: Sec. 8.4.2: sa anumang change sa information, dapat mag-report at magsumite ng related document ang Importer within ten (10) calendar days mula sa occurrence nito.

level1.question: Alin ang minimum na impormasyon na dapat makita sa Geotagged Photos ng office at warehouse/storage area na isinusumite ng bagong applicant?

choices.A: Location address, latitude, longitude, at date and time
choices.B: Location address, latitude, longitude, at pangalan ng photographer
choices.C: Business name, latitude, longitude, at date and time
choices.D: Location address, TIN, latitude, at longitude

level1.reason: Sec. 5.3(p): dapat ipakita ng Geotagged Photos, at the minimum, ang location address (p.1), latitude (p.2), longitude (p.3), at date and time (p.4).

level1.question: Gaano katagal dapat itago ng accredited Importer sa principal place of business nito ang mga related records para sa post clearance audit, mula sa date ng final payment ng duties and taxes o customs clearance?

choices.A: Isang (1) taon
choices.B: Dalawang (2) taon
choices.D: Tatlong (3) taon

level1.reason: Sec. 11.1: kailangang itago ang records sa principal place of business for a period of three (3) years mula sa date ng final payment ng duties and taxes o customs clearance, as the case may be.

level2.question: A Bureau official to whom the Commissioner had delegated the authority to act on applications disapproved the new accreditation application of Apex Trading Corp. The disapproval was not based on misrepresentation of Material Information or on false documents. Apex received the notice of disapproval and wants to contest it. What must Apex do to perfect its remedy?

choices.A: File a Motion for Reconsideration within ten (10) days from receipt, to be resolved within ten (10) days
choices.B: Appeal to the Commissioner within ten (10) calendar days from receipt and pay the Php1,000.00 appeal fee within that period
choices.C: Appeal to the Commissioner within fifteen (15) calendar days from receipt and pay the Php1,000.00 appeal fee within that period
choices.D: Appeal to the Commissioner within fifteen (15) calendar days from receipt, with no appeal fee required

level2.reason: Under Sec. 19.1.2, when the disapproval was issued by an authorized Bureau official (not directly by the Commissioner), the applicant may appeal to the Commissioner within fifteen (15) calendar days from receipt of the notice. The Php1,000.00 appeal fee must be paid within the period of appeal, and no appeal is perfected without it. The ten-day Motion for Reconsideration in Sec. 19.1.1 applies only when the Commissioner directly exercised the disapproval.

level2.question: The accreditation of Luzon Fresh Foods Corp., a private corporation, expired on March 31. It filed its renewal application with complete documents on April 10. Its accreditation had never been suspended. The renewal was approved on April 14, within the period prescribed for acting on the application. Under CAO 07-2022, what late-renewal fine applies and from when is the renewed one-year validity reckoned?

choices.A: A Php2,000.00 fine applies, and the one-year validity is reckoned from April 14
choices.B: A Php1,000.00 fine applies, and the one-year validity is reckoned from April 14
choices.C: A Php2,000.00 fine applies, and the one-year validity is reckoned from April 1
choices.D: No fine applies, and the one-year validity is reckoned from April 1

level2.reason: Under Sec. 6.4, filing after the expiration of the accreditation carries a Php2,000.00 fine; the Php1,000.00 fine is for filing less than seven (7) working days before expiration. Neither exception in Sec. 6.4.1 applies, since the accreditation was not suspended and Luzon Fresh is not a government agency or privileged entity. Under Sec. 6.4.3, the validity period for late applications is reckoned from the date of approval, which is April 14.

level2.question: Harbor Link Imports received a system password after its accreditation was approved. A former staff member used the password to lodge a goods declaration, and the shipment was released. Two weeks later, Harbor Link emailed the Bureau that the lodgement was unauthorized and denied responsibility. Under CAO 07-2022, how will the lodgement be treated?

choices.A: The lodgement is set aside because Harbor Link may invoke good faith in reporting the misuse
choices.B: The lodgement is attributed to the former staff member because passwords are personal to the user
choices.C: The lodgement is held in suspense until the Bureau rules on Harbor Link's belated report
choices.D: The lodgement is conclusively attributable to Harbor Link because no report was made before release

level2.reason: Sec. 8.3 makes the password personal and exclusive to the Importer, who cannot claim good faith or allege unauthorized use. Use of the password is deemed conclusive and attributable to the Importer unless the unauthorized use is reported by email or the Bureau's official hotline before the release of the shipment. Harbor Link reported only after release, so the lodgement is attributed to it.

level2.question: Metro Sourcing Inc., an accredited Third Party Importer, lodged a goods declaration for goods bought by its client, Kalayaan Retail. Metro Sourcing keeps a record of its contract with Kalayaan. However, the bill of lading, invoice, and packing list name only Metro Sourcing and do not indicate that the importation is for the account of another party. How does CAO 07-2022 treat the importation?

choices.A: It is deemed for the account of Kalayaan Retail because Metro Sourcing is a Third Party Importer
choices.B: It is deemed for the own account and benefit of Metro Sourcing because the documents do not indicate otherwise
choices.C: It is deemed for the account of Kalayaan Retail because Metro Sourcing keeps a record of the contract
choices.D: It is deemed a Non-regular Importer transaction of Kalayaan Retail pending submission of corrected documents

level2.reason: Sec. 8.5 requires a Third Party Importer to keep a record of its contract with the ultimate consignee and also requires the supporting documents, such as the bill of lading, invoice, or packing list, to clearly indicate that the importation is for the account of another party. Otherwise, the importation is deemed for the own account and benefit of the Importer. Keeping the contract record alone is not enough.

level2.question: The accreditation of Sunrise Electronics was suspended on June 3. Two of its containers arrived at the port on May 28, and a third is still in transit. Sunrise wants all three shipments processed despite the suspension. What should Sunrise do?

choices.A: Lodge the goods declarations in the automated system because the shipments arrived or departed before the suspension
choices.B: Pay the Php2,000.00 Processing Fee to the AMO so the accreditation is reactivated for these shipments
choices.C: Request the Commissioner, Attention: Legal Service, for continuous processing, accepting 100% physical examination of the goods
choices.D: Request the District Collector for continuous processing, with examination under the selectivity screen

level2.reason: Under Sec. 16.1, an Importer with suspended accreditation cannot lodge or process goods declarations. Sec. 17.1 allows it to request the Commissioner, Attn: Legal Service, for continuous processing of shipments in transit or arrived on or prior to the suspension. Sec. 17.2 requires the request to state that 100% physical examination will be conducted regardless of the selectivity screen, on the Importer's own account.

level2.question: A Warrant of Seizure and Detention was issued against a shipment of restricted goods imported by Pacific Gears Inc., and a thirty (30)-day preliminary suspension of its accreditation was imposed. The thirty days have lapsed, the Commissioner has not extended the suspension, and forfeiture proceedings on the shipment are still pending. What is the status of the suspension?

choices.A: It is lifted only after the forfeiture proceedings are resolved
choices.B: It is automatically lifted because the thirty-day period has lapsed
choices.C: It is automatically lifted because the Commissioner did not extend it for fifteen (15) days
choices.D: It continues for fifteen (15) more days and is then automatically lifted

level2.reason: Sec. 9.1 provides that the thirty-day preliminary suspension is automatically lifted upon lapse of the period, unless extended by the Commissioner for fifteen (15) days on meritorious grounds. The proviso states that where the violation involves prohibited or restricted goods, the lifting, if applicable, is done only after the resolution of the forfeiture proceedings. Since restricted goods are involved and the proceedings are pending, the suspension is not lifted yet.

level2.question: Oriental Cargo Corp. was warned by the Bureau for failing to keep and maintain a signage of its business name at its declared place of business. Months later, a verification again finds no signage. Under Section 13 of CAO 07-2022, what penalty applies to this second violation?

choices.A: Warning to suspension of up to thirty (30) days
choices.B: Suspension from six (6) months and one (1) day to one (1) year
choices.D: Suspension from one (1) month and one (1) day to six (6) months

level2.reason: Failure to keep and maintain a business name signage (Sec. 8.7) is listed under Light Infractions in Sec. 13. The penalty for a second violation is suspension from one (1) month and one (1) day to six (6) months. Warning to suspension up to thirty (30) days is for the first violation, and revocation is for the third.

level2.question: During evaluation of the new application of Greenfield Foods Corp., an AMO evaluator found that the business address in the CPRS differs from the address in the submitted proof of lawful occupancy. The evaluator posted a notice on the BOC portal requiring justification. Seven calendar days after the posting, Greenfield had neither responded nor requested additional time. What is the result?

choices.A: The application is deferred until Greenfield settles any outstanding obligation with the Bureau
choices.B: The application is disapproved, without prejudice to a new application and payment of the corresponding fees
choices.C: The application is disapproved, and Greenfield is barred from transacting with the Bureau
choices.D: The application is returned as incomplete and is not processed until the lacking documents are submitted

level2.reason: Under Sec. 7.3, if evaluation shows discrepancies requiring justification, the applicant must submit it within seven (7) calendar days from posting of the notice. Otherwise the application is disapproved, without prejudice to filing a new application and paying the corresponding fees. The bar from transacting with the Bureau in Sec. 7.4.4 applies to misrepresentation or false documents, which is not the case here.

level2.question: Bayside Imports is applying for automatic renewal of its accreditation and needs clearances from several Bureau offices. It must show that no Warrant of Seizure and Detention has been issued against its shipments, or that any such warrant was resolved in its favor. Which office issues this clearance?

choices.A: Collection Service, Revenue Collection Monitoring Group
choices.B: Legal Service, Revenue Collection Monitoring Group
choices.D: Accounts Management Office

level2.reason: Under Sec. 6.5.4(b), the clearance showing no WSD issued against the Importer's shipments, or that any WSD was resolved in its favor, comes from the Intelligence Group (IG). The Collection Service, RCMG certifies no outstanding liability, and the Legal Service, RCMG certifies no pending case or investigation.

level2.question: Alon Builders Inc. and Dagat Marine Corp. formed a Joint Venture to import equipment and will apply for accreditation as a JV, with Alon Builders as the nominated partner. Which requirement applies to the application under CAO 07-2022?

choices.A: The nominated partner is accredited under its own name without any suffix
choices.B: The accredited name carries the JV acronym as a suffix, and a certified true copy of the JV agreement is attached
choices.C: Only Alon Builders submits the Section 5.3 documents, while Dagat Marine submits none
choices.D: Any employee of either partner may sign the application form without authority from the Principal Officers

level2.reason: Sec. 5.4 requires a certified true copy of the Joint Venture agreement to be attached to the application. Whether the Importer is in the name of the JV entities or the nominated partner, the acronym JV must be suffixed to the registered name. Each partner must also submit the Section 5.3 documents unless already secured for the JV agreement, and the form must be signed by a Responsible Officer authorized by the Principal Officers of the respective partners.

level1.question: Ano ang FOB o FCA value ng Goods of Commercial Nature na dumadaan sa Informal Entry Process?

choices.A: Php10,000.00 o mas mababa
choices.B: Php50,000.00 o higit pa
choices.D: Mas mababa sa Php50,000.00

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 3.16 at 4.1.1, ang Goods of Commercial Nature ay dumadaan sa Informal Entry Process kapag ang FOB o FCA value ay less than Fifty Thousand Pesos (Php50,000.00). Hindi pasok ang value na Php50,000.00 o higit pa, dahil 'less than' ang batayan. Ang Php150,000.00 ay para lang sa coffins o urns sa Sec. 4.1.3(g).

level1.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod ang hindi sakop ng CAO 02-2021 ayon sa Section 1?

choices.A: Goods of commercial nature na may FOB value na mas mababa sa Php50,000.00
choices.B: Personal at household effects na hindi commercial quantity
choices.D: Balikbayan boxes na conditionally tax and/or duty-exempt

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 1, ang CAO ay applicable sa lahat ng importations na dinadaan sa Informal Entry Process, may duty at tax man o wala, maliban sa accompanied baggage, De Minimis importations at relief consignments na may sariling regulations. Ang balikbayan boxes ay sakop sa Sec. 4.1.3(b).

level1.question: Anong proseso ang dapat sundin sa importation ng motor vehicles, motorcycles at motor scooters, kahit pa sakop ito ng Section 800 ng CMTA?

choices.A: Informal Entry Process, basta mas mababa sa Php50,000.00 ang FOB value
choices.B: Formal Entry Process, anuman ang consignee
choices.C: Informal Entry Process, basta Section 800 ng CMTA ang saklaw nito
choices.D: Informal Entry Process, basta personal use ang motor vehicle

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 4.2, ang importation ng motor vehicles, motorcycles at motor scooters ay laging sa Formal Entry Process, regardless of the consignees, kasama ang mga sakop ng Section 800 ng CMTA.

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang calendar days mula sa discharge ng huling package mula sa vessel o aircraft dapat i-lodge ang goods declaration?

choices.A: Labinlimang (15) calendar days
choices.B: Tatlumpung (30) calendar days
choices.D: Tatlong (3) working days

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 5.3, ang goods declaration ay dapat i-lodge within fifteen (15) calendar days mula sa discharge ng last package. Puwedeng i-extend ng another 15 calendar days sa valid grounds kung may written request bago mag-expire ang original period, at walang further extension.

level1.question: Anong form ang ginagamit ng declarant sa pag-file ng goods declaration habang hindi pa implemented ang Informal Entry System?

choices.A: Gate Pass BC Form No. 201
choices.B: Informal Import Declaration and Entry (IIDE) BC Form No. 177
choices.D: Provisional Goods Declaration

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 5.1, habang hindi pa implemented ang Informal Entry System, ang declarant ay gagamit ng Informal Import Declaration and Entry (IIDE) BC Form No. 177. Ang BC Form No. 201 ay Gate Pass (Sec. 5.2.4), at ang BCOR ay ebidensya ng payment (Sec. 5.9).

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang working days dapat aksyunan ang request for extension sa paglo-lodge ng goods declaration, bago ito ituring na deemed approved?

choices.A: Isang (1) working day
choices.B: Limang (5) working days
choices.D: Tatlong (3) working days

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 5.3, ang request for extension ay dapat aksyunan within three (3) working days, kung hindi ay deemed approved ang request.

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang calendar days mula lodgement ng Provisional Goods Declaration dapat isumite ang other supporting documents ayon sa notarized undertaking ng declarant?

choices.A: Apatnapu't limang (45) calendar days
choices.B: Labinlimang (15) calendar days
choices.D: Siyamnapung (90) calendar days

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 5.4.2(d), ang notarized undertaking ng declarant ay nagsasabing isusumite ang other supporting documents within forty-five (45) calendar days mula lodgement ng Provisional Goods Declaration. Puwede itong i-extend ng another 45 days sa valid reasons at approved written request na ginawa bago mag-lapse ang original period.

level1.question: Alin ang mandatory para sa lahat ng containerized cargo sa ilalim ng Informal Entry Process bago ang assessment at payment ng duties at taxes?

choices.A: Physical examination ng lahat ng packages
choices.B: Documentary check lamang
choices.D: Alert Order mula sa competent authority

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 5.6.2(b), mandatory ang x-ray inspection para sa lahat ng containerized cargo sa ilalim ng Informal Entry Process bago ang assessment at payment ng duties at taxes. Physical examination ay isasagawa lang kapag may suspicion of irregularity ang x-ray image.

level1.question: Para sa air shipments, sino ang nag-i-issue ng Bureau of Customs Official Receipt (BCOR) bilang ebidensya ng payment?

choices.A: Ang BOC cashier
choices.B: Ang in-house bank
choices.D: Ang Customs Operations Officer V

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 5.9.2, sa air shipments, ang order of payment ay ipinapakita sa BOC cashier na nag-i-issue ng BCOR. Sa sea shipments naman, ang in-house bank ang nag-i-issue ng BCOR (Sec. 5.9.1).

level1.question: Sino ang puwedeng mag-recommend ng pagtaas o pagbaba ng threshold value ng Goods of Commercial Nature sa Informal Entry Process, at kaninong approval ito nakasalalay?

choices.A: Ang District Collector, subject sa approval ng Commissioner
choices.B: Ang Commissioner, subject sa approval ng Secretary of Finance
choices.C: Ang Secretary of Finance, subject sa approval ng Commissioner
choices.D: Ang Chief, Informal Entry Division, subject sa approval ng District Collector

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 7, ang Commissioner ang puwedeng mag-recommend ng pagtaas o pagbaba ng threshold value ng Goods of Commercial Nature, at kailangan ito ng approval ng Secretary of Finance.

level2.question: Alba Trading brings in two shipments. Shipment 1 is commercial goods with an FOB value of Php47,500.00. Shipment 2 is a motorcycle imported by a returning resident under Section 800 of the CMTA, with an FOB value of Php40,000.00. Which clearance process applies to each shipment under CAO 02-2021?

choices.A: Both shipments are cleared through the Informal Entry Process
choices.B: Both shipments are cleared through the Formal Entry Process
choices.C: Shipment 1 through the Informal Entry Process and Shipment 2 through the Formal Entry Process
choices.D: Shipment 1 through the Formal Entry Process and Shipment 2 through the Informal Entry Process

level2.reason: Under Sec. 4.1.1, commercial goods with FOB or FCA value of less than Php50,000.00 are cleared through the Informal Entry Process, so Shipment 1 (Php47,500.00) qualifies. Sec. 4.2 provides that motor vehicles, motorcycles and motor scooters are processed under the Formal Entry Process regardless of the consignee, including importations under Section 800 of the CMTA. Shipment 2 is therefore Formal Entry even though its value is below Php50,000.00 and it comes from a returning resident.

level2.question: The last package of Orion's shipment was discharged from the vessel on June 5. On June 18, Orion submitted a written request to extend the period to lodge its goods declaration, citing an accident that delayed its documents. The Collector of Customs did not act on the request within three working days. Assume calendar days are counted starting the day after the triggering date. What is the last day Orion may lodge its goods declaration?

choices.A: July 5, the end of the 15-day extension
choices.B: June 20, the end of the original period
choices.D: August 4, 45 days from the end of the original period

level2.reason: Sec. 5.3 requires lodgement within 15 calendar days from discharge of the last package, so the original period ended June 20 (June 5 + 15). The request on June 18 was made before expiration and cited a valid ground (accident, Sec. 5.3.2). A request not acted upon within three working days is deemed approved, and the 15-day extension runs from the day after the original period expired: June 21 to July 5. No further extension is allowed.

level2.question: A customs broker is manually filing a goods declaration at the Informal Entry Division for an air shipment. The declaration is signed by the broker and notarized, and the broker attaches the AWB, the commercial invoice and the packing list. None of the other documents listed in Section 5.2.5 applies to these goods. Which required supporting document is still missing?

choices.A: Tax Exemption Indorsement
choices.B: Authority to Release Imported Goods (ATRIG)
choices.D: Sanitary and Phytosanitary (SPS) certificate

level2.reason: Sec. 5.2 lists the supporting documents: BL/HBL or AWB/HAWB, commercial invoice, packing list, and the Gate Pass BC Form No. 201 for the airport in case of manual filing (Sec. 5.2.4). The broker has the AWB, invoice and packing list and is filing manually for an air shipment, so the Gate Pass is missing. The TEI, ATRIG and SPS certificate are required only as other documents when applicable (Sec. 5.2.5), and none applies here.

level2.question: Kestrel Foods will import regulated goods and filed its application for the required permit with the regulatory agency before the goods arrived, but the permit has not yet been issued. Kestrel wants to lodge a Provisional Goods Declaration. Which set of documents must it present under the CAO?

choices.A: A commercial invoice, a packing list, a Gate Pass BC Form No. 201, and the import permit
choices.B: Only the permit application and a notarized undertaking to submit the remaining documents
choices.C: A Tax Exemption Indorsement, a pro forma invoice, and a written order of the Commissioner
choices.D: A pro forma invoice, a duly endorsed BL or AWB, advance copies of the Certificate of Origin if applicable, and a notarized undertaking

level2.reason: Sec. 5.4.1(a) allows a Provisional Goods Declaration when no regulatory permit has been presented, provided the application was filed before departure or arrival as required. Under Sec. 5.4.2, the documents to present are a pro forma invoice, a duly endorsed BL or AWB (or the carrier's written order if none), advance copies of the Certificate of Origin if applicable, and a duly notarized undertaking to submit the other documents within 45 calendar days. The permit itself is not required at this stage.

level2.question: Meridian Pharma, an importer enrolled in a Bureau trade facilitation program, lodged a Provisional Goods Declaration for regulated goods because its permit has not yet been issued. The concerned regulatory agency allows conditional release of the goods. Which conditions apply to the release?

choices.A: The goods may be sold once duties are paid, and no security is required because Meridian is enrolled
choices.B: The goods are stored at Meridian's premises and not disposed of until the permit is submitted, and a general security or undertaking may replace a specific security
choices.C: The goods are held at the Off-dock CFW until the permit is submitted, and a specific security is required in every case
choices.D: The goods are released only after the declaration is converted to a formal entry, with a general security posted

level2.reason: Sec. 5.4.4(a) governs conditional release of regulated shipments under a Provisional Goods Declaration: the regulatory agency must allow the release; the goods are delivered to the importer's premises for storage and may not be disposed of until the permit, clearance or license is issued and submitted within the prescribed period; and a specific and sufficient security is required, except that for importers enrolled in a trade facilitation program a general security or an undertaking may be required instead. Meridian is enrolled, so a general security or undertaking may replace the specific security.

level2.question: Pinnacle Imports obtained conditional release of its goods under a Provisional Goods Declaration because it lacked an invoice needed to assess the correct duties, and it posted a security covering the possible duties and taxes. Pinnacle did not submit the invoice within the prescribed period and requested no extension. The Bureau gave Pinnacle due notice. What is the consequence for the security?

choices.A: The security is automatically returned because the goods were already released
choices.B: The security is held until Pinnacle lodges a new Provisional Goods Declaration
choices.C: The security is subject to forfeiture, without prejudice to other legal remedies to recover duties and taxes due
choices.D: The security is cancelled and the goods are seized instead, as with missing regulatory permits

level2.reason: Sec. 5.4.5(b) provides that when goods are released under a Provisional Goods Declaration because of lacking import documents needed to assess the correct duties, any security posted or undertaking submitted is subject to forfeiture if the required documents are not submitted within the prescribed period, provided due notice is given and without prejudice to other legal remedies. Seizure under Sec. 5.4.5(a) applies to regulated goods lacking the required permit, not to this case.

level2.question: Lumen Corp lodged a Provisional Goods Declaration on August 1 with a notarized undertaking to submit the missing documents within 45 calendar days. Before the 45-day period lapsed, Lumen filed a written request for extension based on the same ground as the Provisional Goods Declaration, and the Collector of Customs approved it. Assume days are counted starting the day after the lodgement or lapse date. What is the last day Lumen may submit the missing documents?

choices.A: October 30, which is 90 days from lodgement
choices.B: September 15, which is 45 days from lodgement
choices.C: September 30, which is 15 days after the original period lapsed
choices.D: November 14, which is 105 days from lodgement
