level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.4.2(d), the undertaking is to submit the other documents within 45 calendar days from lodgement, extendable for another 45 days for valid reasons upon approved written request made before the original period lapses. Lodgement on August 1: August 1 + 45 days = September 15; September 15 + 45 days = October 30, which is also 90 days from lodgement. The 15-day extension in Sec. 5.3 concerns lodging the goods declaration, not this period.

level2.question: A diplomatic agent's personal shipment arrives, and a Customs Officer proposes to physically examine it. There are no serious grounds to believe that the shipment contains articles outside the exemptions under Article 36, paragraph 1 of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, and its importation is neither prohibited by law nor controlled by Philippine quarantine regulations. How should the Bureau treat the shipment?

choices.A: It must be physically examined, since all informal entry shipments are subject to inspection
choices.B: It is exempt from inspection because there are no serious grounds to justify examining it
choices.C: It may be physically examined without notice if the diplomatic agent is not available
choices.D: It may be x-rayed only, without the presence of the diplomatic agent or representative

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.6.2(d), the personal baggage or shipments of a diplomatic agent are exempt from inspection unless there are serious grounds to believe they contain articles outside the Article 36(1) exemptions of the Vienna Convention, or the articles are prohibited by law or controlled by quarantine regulations. No such grounds exist here, so the shipment is exempt. Any permitted inspection must be done in the presence of the diplomatic agent or an authorized representative.

level2.question: Pending full automation, the Customs Operations Officer V (COO V) of the port verified the BCOR presented by a customs broker in the electronic payment system and confirmed that payment was made. The COO V stamped Payment Verified on the white and green copies of the BCOR. What happens next so the goods can be released?

choices.A: The COO V electronically transmits the release instruction directly to the terminal facility operator
choices.B: The broker presents the stamped copies directly to the terminal facility operator for release
choices.C: The Chief, Informal Entry Division issues a new goods declaration that triggers the release instruction
choices.D: The COO V forwards the stamped copies to the Chief, Informal Entry Division, who performs the Manual Discharge that triggers the release instruction

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.10, pending full automation the COO V verifies the BCOR, stamps Payment Verified on the white and green copies, and forwards them to the Chief, Informal Entry Division or equivalent unit. The Chief then performs the Manual Discharge in the e-manifest, which triggers the electronic release instruction to the terminal facility operator or Off-dock CFW. The COO V does not transmit the release instruction directly.

level2.question: A customs broker lodges an informal entry for goods using a falsified commercial invoice that understates the value of the goods. The Bureau discovers the false statement. Under CAO 02-2021, which provisions govern the sanctions?

choices.A: Sanctions and penalties under Section 1401, Chapter 1, Title XIV of the CMTA and other applicable penal provisions
choices.B: Only the forfeiture of any security posted under the Provisional Goods Declaration rules
choices.C: Only the review of the broker's lodgement privileges by the Informal Entry Division
choices.D: The abandonment rules under Chapter 6, Title XI of the CMTA

level2.reason: Sec. 9 provides that any person who makes or attempts to lodge, process and clear imported goods by false or fraudulent statements is subject to the sanctions and penalties under Section 1401, Chapter 1, Title XIV of the CMTA and other applicable penal provisions. A falsified invoice that understates value is a false statement in lodging an informal entry. Forfeiture of Provisional Goods Declaration security (Sec. 5.4.5) and abandonment (Sec. 5.5) address different situations.

level1.question: Ano ang sakop ng CAO 02-2020 ayon sa Section 1?

choices.A: Ang proseso ng seizure at forfeiture ng goods na sadyang na-misdeclare
choices.B: Ang administrative remedies ng aggrieved importer o exporter sa dispute settlement o protest tungkol sa valuation, rules of origin, tariff classification at iba pang customs issues
choices.C: Ang pag-apela ng customs broker laban sa pagkansela ng kanyang accreditation
choices.D: Ang pag-issue ng Advance Ruling ng Bureau at ng Tariff Commission bago ang importation

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 1 (Scope), sakop ng CAO ang right to administrative remedies ng aggrieved importer o exporter sa dispute settlement o protest na galing sa customs valuation, rules of origin, tariff classification at other customs issues. Hindi nito sakop ang seizure at forfeiture proceedings, accreditation appeals, o ang pag-issue ng Advance Ruling.

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang araw dapat mag-file ng protest sa Commissioner ang aggrieved importer mula sa pagtanggap ng adverse ruling ng District Collector?

choices.A: Pitong (7) araw
choices.B: Sampung (10) araw
choices.D: Tatlumpung (30) araw

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 10.1, ang protest ay dapat i-file in writing sa Commissioner within fifteen (15) days mula pagtanggap ng adverse ruling ng District Collector (o mula sa payment kung may binayaran dahil sa ruling). Kapag lumampas, final and conclusive na ang action ng District Collector.

level1.question: Ano ang epekto kapag hindi kumilos ang Commissioner sa isang protest na proper ang form sa loob ng tatlumpung (30) araw mula pagtanggap nito?

choices.A: Ituturing na affirmed ang ruling ng Collector
choices.B: Ituturing na reversed ang ruling ng Collector at pabor ito sa importer
choices.C: Awtomatikong ililipat ang protest sa Tariff Commission
choices.D: Awtomatikong ire-release ang goods nang walang Security

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 10.3, kapag proper ang form ng protest, dapat mag-rule ang Commissioner within thirty (30) days mula pagtanggap. Kapag hindi siya kumilos, ang ruling ng Collector ay deemed affirmed.

level1.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod ang hindi itinuturing na Protestable Case ayon sa Section 3.8?

choices.A: Adverse ruling ng District Collector sa tariff classification
choices.B: Adverse ruling ng District Collector sa customs valuation
choices.C: Adverse ruling ng District Collector sa rules of origin
choices.D: Pagtatakda ng District Collector ng fines sa seizure cases

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 3.8, ang Protestable Case ay anumang ruling o decision ng District Collector na adverse sa importer, consignee o exporter, maliban sa fixing of fines in seizure cases. Kaya protestable ang adverse rulings sa classification, valuation at rules of origin (Sec. 10.1), pero hindi ang pagtatakda ng fines sa seizure cases.

level1.question: Ano ang kailangang gawin ng importer para ma-release ang goods under Tentative Assessment sa isang difficult o highly technical na tariff classification issue?

choices.A: Mag-post lamang ng Security at hindi na kailangang bayaran ang duties at taxes na declared
choices.B: Bayaran ang duties at taxes ayon sa goods declaration at mag-post ng sufficient Security para sa disputed amount
choices.C: Bayaran ang buong duties at taxes ayon sa reclassification ng Customs Officer at mag-file agad ng protest
choices.D: Bayaran ang kalahati ng disputed amount at mag-post ng Security para sa natitirang kalahati

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 5.4.3, ang importer ay puwedeng humiling ng release under Tentative Assessment kapag binayaran niya ang duties at taxes as declared sa goods declaration at nag-post ng sufficient Security para sa disputed amount, bukod sa pagsunod sa iba pang applicable rules. Ang pagbabayad ayon sa reclassification ng Customs Officer ay ang directive sa Sec. 5.5, hindi ang tentative release.

level1.question: Kapag hindi sang-ayon ang importer sa reclassification ng Customs Officer, sino ang susunod na pagdadalhan ng usapin pagkatapos ng principal appraiser?

choices.A: Ang Chief, Formal Entry Division o equivalent unit
choices.B: Ang Deputy Collector for Assessment
choices.D: Ang Tariff Commission

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 5.1, ang pagkakasunod-sunod ng elevation ay Customs Officer, principal appraiser, Chief, Formal Entry Division o equivalent unit, Deputy Collector for Assessment, at huli ang District Collector. Kaya ang Chief, Formal Entry Division ang kasunod ng principal appraiser.

level1.question: Kailan itinuturing na difficult o highly technical ang Tariff Classification Issue ayon sa Section 5.3?

choices.A: Kapag hindi sumasang-ayon ang importer sa reclassification ng Customs Officer
choices.B: Kapag may pending Advance Ruling application ang goods sa Tariff Commission
choices.C: Kapag classifiable ang goods sa higit sa isang AHTN chapter, heading o subheading
choices.D: Kapag may spurious document na isinumite kasama ng goods declaration

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 5.3.1, difficult o highly technical ang tariff classification issue kapag classifiable ang goods sa higit sa isang AHTN chapter, heading o subheading. Ang Sec. 5.3.2 ay nagdadagdag ng kasong hindi specifically provided ang product description sa anumang AHTN heading o subheading. Ang simpleng hindi pagsang-ayon sa reclassification ay hindi sapat.

level1.question: Sa valuation dispute na difficult o highly technical, sa loob ng ilang araw mula pagtanggap ng notice dapat magsumite ng position papers ang importer at ang Customs Officer?

choices.A: Dalawang (2) araw
choices.B: Tatlong (3) araw
choices.D: Limang (5) araw

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 6.2.2, sa valuation issue na difficult o highly technical, ipinag-uutos ng District Collector na magsumite ng position papers ang importer at ang Customs Officer within five (5) days mula pagtanggap ng notice.

level1.question: Saan ipinapasa ng District Collector ang Certificate of Origin para sa verification mula sa issuing country?

choices.A: Sa Tariff Commission
choices.B: Sa Technical Committee ng Bureau
choices.C: Sa Assessment and Operations Coordinating Group (AOCG)
choices.D: Sa Court of Tax Appeals

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 7.3, ipinapasa ng District Collector ang Certificate of Origin (CO) sa Assessment and Operations Coordinating Group (AOCG) para sa verification mula sa issuing country.

level1.question: Magkano ang surcharge na ipapataw kapag intentional o fraudulent ang misdeclaration, misclassification o undervaluation?

choices.A: 500% ng duty at tax na due
choices.B: 250% ng duty at tax na due
choices.C: 100% ng duty at tax na due
choices.D: 50% ng duty at tax na due

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 4.7, kapag intentional o fraudulent ang misdeclaration, misclassification o undervaluation, hindi na applicable ang dispute settlement at Section 1400 ng CMTA ang susundin. May surcharge na 500% ng duty at tax na due, at subject sa seizure ang goods anuman ang laki ng discrepancy.

level2.question: On March 3, Delta Imports received the District Collector's written ruling, adverse to Delta on a valuation issue. On March 10, Delta paid the duties and taxes demanded as a result of that ruling. Assume each period is counted starting the day after the triggering event and that no holidays or weekends affect the count. What is the last day Delta may file a written protest with the Commissioner?

choices.A: March 18, which is 15 days from receipt of the ruling
choices.B: March 25, which is 15 days from the payment
choices.C: April 2, which is 30 days from receipt of the ruling
choices.D: April 9, which is 30 days from the payment

level2.reason: Under Sec. 10.1, a protest must be filed in writing with the Commissioner within 15 days from receipt of the adverse ruling or, when payment is made as a result of the ruling, within 15 days from that payment. Delta paid on March 10 because of the ruling, so the period runs from payment: March 10 + 15 days = March 25. Otherwise, the District Collector's action becomes final and conclusive.

level2.question: A District Collector determined that a valuation issue involving Meridian Trading is difficult and highly technical, and required position papers. Meridian and the Customs Officer both submitted their position papers on May 10. Assume the period is counted starting the day after submission and no holidays apply. By what date must the District Collector resolve the valuation issue in writing?

choices.A: May 12
choices.B: May 15
choices.D: June 9

level2.reason: Sec. 6.2.5 requires the District Collector to resolve a difficult or highly technical Valuation Issue in writing within 15 days from submission of the position papers. Position papers were submitted on May 10, so May 10 + 15 days = May 25. The 2-day and 5-day periods in Secs. 6.2.1 and 6.2.2 concern the notice and the position papers, not the resolution.

level2.question: Solaris Foods imported goods claiming a preferential rate under a Certificate of Origin whose authenticity the Customs Officer questioned. Solaris disagreed, requested verification, and obtained release of the goods under Tentative Assessment by paying the declared duties and posting a cash bond covering the disputed amount. The issuing country then reported that the Certificate of Origin was not authentic. What must the District Collector do with the cash bond?

choices.A: Forfeit the cash bond posted by Solaris
choices.B: Cancel the cash bond and apply the preferential rate
choices.C: Refund the cash bond pending a Tariff Commission ruling
choices.D: Hold the cash bond until the Court of Tax Appeals rules

level2.reason: Under Sec. 7.5.2, if the issuing country finds that the Certificate of Origin was not authentic or accurate, the District Collector forfeits the Security posted in case of a cash bond (or requires payment of the disputed duties and taxes). Solaris posted a cash bond (Sec. 7.4), so the bond is forfeited. Cancellation of the bond and application of the preferential rate happen only if the CO is confirmed as authentic or accurate (Sec. 7.5.1).

level2.question: While a tariff classification dispute involving Orion Imports is pending before the District Collector, the Customs Officer discovers that Orion submitted a forged invoice, resulting in an assessment lower than what is legally due. What should happen to the dispute settlement proceedings?

choices.A: The proceedings continue, and Orion may still obtain release under Tentative Assessment by posting Security
choices.B: The proceedings are suspended until the Tariff Commission rules on the classification
choices.C: The proceedings are elevated to the Commissioner as a protest filed by the Bureau
choices.D: The proceedings are terminated, and a Warrant of Seizure and Detention is issued against the shipment

level2.reason: Sec. 4.7 states that when fraud is discovered at any stage of a dispute settlement that has already commenced, an enforcement issue is deemed to have arisen, the proceedings are terminated, and a Warrant of Seizure and Detention is issued against the shipment. A forged invoice that lowers the assessed duties and taxes is the type of fraudulent document the provision describes.

level2.question: A Customs Officer challenges the declaration of Kappa Corp. on a customs issue that is not about tariff classification, valuation or rules of origin but affects the assessment of duties and taxes. The officer questions the genuineness of a supporting document submitted with the goods declaration. Kappa offers to pay the declared duties and post sufficient Security to obtain release under Tentative Assessment. How should this request be treated?

choices.A: Allowed, because the Security covers the disputed amount
choices.B: Allowed, but only if a cash bond is posted instead of other Security
choices.C: Not allowed, because the issue involves the genuineness of a supporting document
choices.D: Not allowed, because Tentative Assessment is available only for tariff classification issues

level2.reason: Sec. 8.2.3 allows release under Tentative Assessment for other customs issues only if the issue does not involve the integrity, authenticity or genuineness of any document submitted in support of the goods declaration. Here the Customs Officer questions the genuineness of a supporting document, so the request cannot be granted even if Kappa pays the declared duties and posts Security.

level2.question: Vega Imports faces a mixed dispute on tariff classification, customs valuation and another customs issue affecting assessment. The District Collector sent the classification question to the Tariff Commission and determined that the correct classification is indispensable to resolving the valuation issue, but not the other customs issue. What may the District Collector do?

choices.A: Resolve all three issues now, since mixed issues are resolved simultaneously
choices.B: Resolve the other customs issue now, but the valuation issue only after the Tariff Commission's ruling
choices.C: Resolve none of the issues until the Tariff Commission rules on classification
choices.D: Resolve the valuation issue now, but the other customs issue only after the Tariff Commission's ruling

level2.reason: Under Sec. 9.1, mixed issues are resolved simultaneously following the procedures for each issue. Sec. 9.2 adds that the District Collector may resolve the other issues without waiting for the Tariff Commission, but when tariff classification is indispensable to resolving another issue such as valuation, that issue is resolved only after the classification ruling is received. The other customs issue does not depend on classification, so it may be resolved now, while the valuation issue must wait.

level2.question: Hartwell Imports received adverse rulings from the District Collector on Goods Declaration A, which involved both a valuation issue and a tariff classification issue, and on Goods Declaration B, which involved a separate valuation issue. Hartwell wants to contest both rulings on all issues by protest within the prescribed period. Which approach complies with Section 10?

choices.A: File one protest covering both Goods Declarations and all issues raised
choices.B: File two protests on Goods Declaration A, one per issue, and none on Goods Declaration B
choices.C: File one protest on Goods Declaration A raising only one issue, and another on Goods Declaration B
choices.D: File one protest on Goods Declaration A raising both issues, and a separate protest on Goods Declaration B

level2.reason: Sec. 10.2 limits the scope of a protest to the particular goods subject of a goods declaration, but any number of issues may be raised for that goods declaration. Hartwell may therefore raise both issues in one protest on Goods Declaration A, but the ruling on Goods Declaration B concerns a different goods declaration and needs its own protest.

level2.question: On July 1, Zen Imports received the Commissioner's adverse ruling on a protest over tariff classification. Zen wants to file a Motion for Reconsideration with the Commissioner. How does the CAO treat this plan?

choices.A: No, because the Motion for Reconsideration is not available for a ruling on tariff classification
choices.B: Yes, within fifteen (15) calendar days from receipt of the ruling
choices.C: Yes, within thirty (30) days from receipt, as with an appeal to the Court of Tax Appeals
choices.D: No, because only the Secretary of Finance may reconsider the Commissioner's ruling

level2.reason: Sec. 11 allows a Motion for Reconsideration within 15 calendar days only for a ruling of the Commissioner other than a ruling on tariff classification. Since Zen's ruling is on tariff classification, the motion is not available. Under Sec. 5.8, Zen may instead submit the matter to the Tariff Commission within 15 days from receipt or appeal to the CTA within 30 days from receipt.

level2.question: On September 1, Rho Trading received the Commissioner's adverse ruling on a valuation protest. Rho filed no Motion for Reconsideration and took no other action. On October 15, Rho files an appeal with the Court of Tax Appeals. Assume days are counted starting the day after receipt. What is the status of the Commissioner's ruling?

choices.A: Still appealable, because the period to appeal to the CTA is 60 days
choices.B: Still appealable, because the Commissioner has not yet acted on a Motion for Reconsideration
choices.C: Final and executory, because the appeal was filed beyond the 30-day period
choices.D: Final and executory only after the Secretary of Finance confirms it

level2.reason: Sec. 13 allows an appeal to the CTA within 30 days from receipt of the Commissioner's adverse decision, and Sec. 12 makes the ruling final and executory unless an appeal is made within that period. Rho received the ruling on September 1, so the period ended on October 1 (September 1 + 30 days). An appeal on October 15 is out of time, and no Motion for Reconsideration was filed.

level2.question: Nova Chemicals obtained release of imported goods under Tentative Assessment after paying the declared duties and taxes and posting a surety bond for the disputed amount. The Tariff Commission later ruled that the goods fall under a heading with a higher tariff rate. No other issues are involved, and the Bureau does not appeal the ruling to the Secretary of Finance. What must the District Collector do?

choices.A: Collect the additional duties and taxes resulting from the higher tariff rate
choices.B: Cancel the surety bond and refund the duties and taxes already paid
choices.C: Issue a Warrant of Seizure and Detention against the goods
choices.D: Refer the matter to the Court of Tax Appeals for collection

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.4.4, upon the Tariff Commission's ruling the goods are finally assessed unless other issues are involved or the Bureau appeals to the Secretary of Finance. Here neither exists, and the ruling classifies the goods under a higher tariff rate, so the District Collector collects the additional duties and taxes. Refund of the cash bond or cancellation of the surety bond applies only when the ruling is not for a higher rate.

level1.question: Ano ang sakop ng CAO 05-2020 ayon sa Section 1?

choices.A: Lahat ng air cargo na dumarating sa international airports sa Pilipinas
choices.B: Express Shipments na dala bilang cargo sa ilalim ng MAWB na naka-consign sa AECO
choices.C: Express Shipments na dala sa ilalim ng HAWB na naka-consign sa ultimate consignee
choices.D: Consolidated shipments na dumarating sa Pilipinas sa pamamagitan ng sea freight

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 1 (Scope), sakop ng CAO ang Express Shipments na dala bilang cargo sa ilalim ng Master Air Waybill (MAWB) na naka-consign sa Air Express Cargo Operators (AECO). Hindi ito sumasaklaw sa lahat ng air cargo, at ang batayan ay MAWB at hindi HAWB.

level1.question: Ano ang House Air Waybill (HAWB) ayon sa Section 3?

choices.A: Air waybill na ini-issue ng air carrier sa international air freight forwarder o consolidator
choices.B: Manifest ng lahat ng individual shipments sa consolidation na isinusumite bilang rider ng inward foreign manifest
choices.C: Electronic na pagpapadala ng freight information sa Bureau bago dumating ang shipment sa port of entry
choices.D: Air waybill para sa isang individual shipment na ini-issue ng freight forwarder o consolidator sa consignor o sender

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 3.10, ang HAWB ay air waybill na sumasaklaw sa isang single, individual shipment o consignment at ini-issue ng freight forwarder o consolidator sa consignor o sender. Ang choice A ay ang MAWB (Sec. 3.11), ang B ay ang CIFCM (Sec. 3.3), at ang C ay ang e-IFCM (Sec. 3.4).

level1.question: Ilang oras bago dumating ang aircraft dapat maipadala ng AECO ang e-IFCM kung ang shipment ay galing sa continent maliban sa Asia?

choices.A: Hindi bababa sa apat (4) na oras
choices.B: Hindi bababa sa isang (1) oras
choices.C: Hindi bababa sa anim (6) na oras
choices.D: Hindi bababa sa dalawampu't apat (24) na oras

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 5.1.2, ang mga galing sa continents maliban sa Asia ay dapat may e-IFCM na naipadala at least four (4) hours bago dumating ang aircraft. Ang isang (1) oras ay para lang sa galing Asia (Sec. 5.1.1).

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang oras mula pagdating ng aircraft dapat isumite ang supplemental manifest para sa cargoes na hindi nakalista sa IFCM?

choices.A: Isang (1) oras
choices.B: Apat (4) na oras
choices.D: Dalawampu't apat (24) na oras

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 5.4, ang cargoes na hindi nakalista sa IFCM ay dapat saklawin ng supplemental manifest na isusumite sa loob ng six (6) hours mula pagdating ng aircraft.

level1.question: Alin ang tamang paglalarawan sa High-Value goods ayon sa Section 3.9?

choices.A: Goods na may FOB o FCA value na higit sa Php10,000.00 pero mas mababa sa Php50,000.00
choices.B: Goods na commercial ang nature at may FOB o FCA value na Php50,000.00 o higit pa
choices.C: Goods na may FOB o FCA value na Php10,000.00 o mas mababa
choices.D: Goods na may FOB o FCA value na lampas lang sa Php50,000.00, hindi kasama ang eksaktong Php50,000.00

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 3.9, ang High-Value ay goods of a commercial nature na may FOB o FCA value na Php50,000.00 or over, kaya kasama ang eksaktong Php50,000.00. Ito rin ang nakasaad sa Sec. 6.4 (Php50,000.00 and above). Ang choice A ay Low-Value (Sec. 6.3) at ang C ay De Minimis.

level1.question: Saan dapat ilagay ang lahat ng Correspondence and Documents ayon sa Section 6.1.4?

choices.A: Sa sealed green courier bag
choices.B: Sa sealed red courier bag
choices.D: Sa sealed blue courier bag

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 6.1.4, ang lahat ng Correspondence and Documents ay dapat ilagay sa sealed green courier bag. Mahalaga ang parehong kulay (green) at ang seal.

level1.question: Sino ang dapat tumiyak na kumpleto ang kinakailangang bilang ng personnel para sa operasyon ng AECO?

choices.A: Ang Deputy Collector for Operations
choices.B: Ang Customs Examiner
choices.D: Ang District Collector

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 4, ang District Collector ang dapat tumiyak na fully complemented ng required number of personnel ang operations ng AECO. Ang Bureau naman ang magbibigay ng overtime services kapag kailangan.

level1.question: Magkano ang pinakamababang halaga na dapat i-deposit at i-maintain ng AECO sa AAB bilang security deposit para sa Low-value, Dutiable and/or Taxable Express Shipments?
level1.reason: Sa Sec. 11, ang AECO ay dapat mag-deposit at mag-maintain sa AAB ng not less than Five Million Pesos (Php5,000,000.00) bilang guaranty ng immediate payment ng bangko kapag hiningi ng Bureau.

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang oras mula pagdating ng shipment dapat i-re-export ng AECO ang mis-sorted o misrouted shipment na ibabalik sa shipper?

choices.A: Dalawampu't apat (24) na oras
choices.B: Anim (6) na oras
choices.D: Pitumpu't dalawang (72) oras

level1.reason: Ayon sa Sec. 10, ang AECO ay dapat mag-re-export ng mis-sorted o misrouted shipment within twenty-four (24) hours from the arrival of the shipment.

level1.question: Ano ang tamang kahulugan ng Restricted Goods ayon sa Section 3.15?

choices.A: Goods na papayagan lang i-import o i-export matapos makuha ang kinakailangang clearances at licenses
choices.B: Goods na ipinagbabawal i-import at i-export nang walang anumang exception
choices.C: Goods na papayagan i-import basta nabayaran na ang duty at tax bago ang release
choices.D: Goods na ipinagbabawal i-import at i-export, maliban kapag pinahintulutan ng batas o regulasyon

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 3.15, ang Restricted Goods ay goods na ipinagbabawal i-import at i-export, except when authorized by law or regulation. Ang choice A ay Regulated Goods (Sec. 3.14) at ang B ay Prohibited Goods (Sec. 3.13).

level2.question: A flight carrying an AECO's consolidated Express Shipments from Tokyo is scheduled to land at 10:00 AM. The AECO electronically sent the e-IFCM at 8:30 AM on the same day, and the e-CIFCM is to be submitted as a rider to it. Assuming the aircraft lands at 10:00 AM as scheduled, by what time should the e-CIFCM be submitted?

choices.A: By 9:00 AM, one hour before the aircraft lands
choices.B: By 10:00 AM, at the time the aircraft lands
choices.C: By 11:00 AM, one hour after the aircraft lands
choices.D: By 2:00 PM, four hours after the aircraft lands

level2.reason: Tokyo is in Asia, so the e-IFCM must be sent at least one hour before arrival (Sec. 5.1.1), meaning by 9:00 AM. Sending it at 8:30 AM is within the prescribed period. Under Sec. 5.3.1, when the e-IFCM is submitted within the prescribed period, the e-CIFCM is submitted one hour after arrival, so 10:00 AM + 1 hour = 11:00 AM.

level2.question: After an aircraft carrying an AECO's consolidation landed at 2:00 PM, the AECO found that three packages were not listed in the IFCM. At 9:30 PM the same day, it submitted a supplemental IFCM covering the packages in both hard copy and electronic form. What is the status of the three packages under the CAO?

choices.A: They are treated as manifested because both forms were submitted on the day of arrival
choices.B: They are treated as unmanifested and subject to seizure proceedings because the six-hour period was exceeded
choices.C: They are treated as manifested once the AECO pays the fines under the CAO on Vessel and Aircraft Supervision and Control System
choices.D: They are treated as Low-Value shipments and released upon posting of a bank guaranty as security deposit

level2.reason: Sec. 5.4 requires the supplemental manifest within six hours upon arrival, so the deadline was 8:00 PM. Submission at 9:30 PM was 7.5 hours after landing, which is late. Under Sec. 5.5, a supplemental IFCM not submitted within the prescribed period makes the shipments unmanifested and subject to seizure proceedings. Submitting both forms does not cure the lateness.

level2.question: Express Shipment X, a commercial parcel under a MAWB consigned to an AECO, has an FOB value of exactly Php10,000.00. Express Shipment Y, also commercial, has an FOB value of exactly Php50,000.00. How should X and Y be classified under the CAO?

choices.A: X is De Minimis and Y is Low-Value
choices.B: X is Low-Value and Y is Low-Value
choices.C: X is Low-Value and Y is High-Value
choices.D: X is De Minimis and Y is High-Value

level2.reason: Under Sec. 6.2, De Minimis covers FOB or FCA value of Php10,000.00 or less, so X is De Minimis. Low-Value under Sec. 6.3 requires value of more than Php10,000.00 but less than Php50,000.00, which excludes both X and Y. High-Value under Secs. 3.9 and 6.4 is Php50,000.00 and above, so Y is High-Value.

level2.question: Two non-document, low-value Express Shipments arrive on the same flight. Both appear on the CIFCM as sent by the same shipper to the same consignee and are valued at USD 450 and USD 430. When the goods were ordered, the exchange rate was Php55.00 per USD, but on the date the shipments arrived it was Php57.50 per USD. How should the Bureau treat the two shipments?

choices.A: As a single consignment requiring formal entry, because their aggregate value on the arrival date is Php50,600.00
choices.B: As two separate Low-Value shipments, because their aggregate value at the ordering rate is only Php48,400.00
choices.C: As two separate Low-Value shipments, because each shipment is valued below Php50,000.00 on the arrival date
choices.D: As a single consignment cleared under informal entry, because each shipment is individually Low-Value

level2.reason: Sec. 8 treats two or more low value non-document express consignments with the same shipper and consignee as a single consignment requiring formal entry if their aggregate value is Php50,000.00 or more, using the foreign currency equivalent at the date of arrival. Calculation: USD 450 + USD 430 = USD 880; USD 880 x Php57.50 = Php50,600.00, which is at least Php50,000.00. The ordering-date rate (USD 880 x Php55.00 = Php48,400.00) is not the applicable rate.

level2.question: Brightline Express, an AECO, wants to release a Low-Value shipment valued at Php35,000.00 before paying the assessed duties and taxes. It has posted a bank guaranty as its security deposit, its informal entry has been filed and processed, and the examination has been completed with duties, taxes and charges properly determined. The aggregate assessed charges are within the amount guaranteed by the AAB, and no alert or hold order has been issued by the Alerting Unit. Which requirement under the CAO still remains?

choices.A: Payment of the assessed duties, taxes and other charges before the shipment is released
choices.B: Filing of a formal entry for the shipment through the Customs Cargo Clearance System
choices.C: Submission to the District Collector of a notarized written commitment executed by an AAB
choices.D: Posting of a new Php5,000,000.00 security deposit exclusively for this single shipment

level2.reason: Sec. 6.3.3 allows release before payment for Low-Value shipments valued below Php50,000.00 upon a bank guaranty, provided five conditions are present: (a) informal entry filed and processed, (b) examination done and charges determined, (c) aggregate charges within the guaranteed amount, (d) no alert or hold order, and (e) the AECO submits to the District Collector a notarized written commitment executed by an AAB. Conditions (a) to (d) are already met, so only (e) remains. Payment before release and formal entry are not required under this provision.

level2.question: A parcel in an AECO's consolidation has an AWB showing a consignee address in Manila, but its labels clearly show a destination in Jakarta, which the Bureau has verified. The AECO informed the Bureau of the error only on the day after the shipment arrived and after the goods declaration had been lodged. The parcel is not under any alert order and is not regulated, restricted or prohibited. May the parcel be returned to the shipper without payment of duties, taxes and other charges under Section 10?

choices.A: Yes, because the labels clearly show a destination outside the Philippines and the Bureau verified it
choices.B: No, because the Bureau was not notified before the shipment arrived and before the goods declaration was lodged
choices.C: Yes, because the parcel is not under an alert order and is not regulated, restricted or prohibited
choices.D: No, because only shipments whose AWB shows a consignee address outside the Philippines may be returned

level2.reason: Sec. 10.2 covers a case where the AWB shows a Philippine address but the labels clearly show a foreign destination verified by the Bureau, so choice D is wrong. However, Sec. 10.3 also requires that the Bureau be notified prior to the arrival of the shipment and lodgment of the goods declaration. Here the notification came after both, so the circumstances for return without duties and taxes are not complete, even though Secs. 10.2 and 10.4 are satisfied.

level2.question: Lumina Express presents a carton of garments declared as 'of no commercial value, Php8,000.00 for customs purposes only' and asks that it be released immediately as an Express Shipment. No invoice or receipt is attached. How does the CAO treat this importation?

choices.A: It is not entitled to immediate release because the declaration is qualified by the phrase 'for customs purposes'
choices.B: It is released as De Minimis because the declared amount does not exceed Php10,000.00
choices.C: It is released after the AECO files a simplified goods declaration before the goods arrive
choices.D: It is released once the AECO posts a bank guaranty acting as the security deposit under Section 11

level2.reason: Sec. 14.1 excludes from immediate release importations declared as 'without commercial value' or 'of no commercial value', or with a specific amount qualified by the phrase 'for customs purposes' or analogous phrases. The declaration here uses both qualifiers, so the carton is not entitled to immediate release as an Express Shipment. The sender, importer, consignee or AECO must instead declare the specific value supported by available invoice, receipt or equivalent document. The De Minimis, simplified declaration and bank guaranty options all presuppose a shipment entitled to immediate release.

level2.question: Orchid Express, an AECO, received under its MAWB a parcel of gold jewelry with an FOB value of Php45,000.00. It wants the parcel cleared as a Low-Value, Dutiable and/or Taxable Express Shipment with advanced processing. Based on the CAO, how should the parcel be treated?

choices.A: It qualifies as Low-Value, Dutiable and/or Taxable because its FOB value is above Php10,000.00 but below Php50,000.00
choices.B: It qualifies as High-Value because jewelry must always be processed under formal entry regardless of value
choices.C: It is excluded from immediate release only because it is a Regulated Good requiring a regulatory agency permit
choices.D: It is not considered an Express Shipment because valuable goods such as jewelry are expressly excluded

level2.reason: Sec. 15.3 lists valuable goods such as jewelry, works of art and the like among those that shall not be considered Express Shipments. Because the parcel is not an Express Shipment, the value-based categories in Sec. 6 do not apply to it, even though Php45,000.00 falls within the Low-Value range of Sec. 6.3. The CAO does not classify jewelry as High-Value or as a Regulated Good.

level2.question: Kestrel Air Express applies for accreditation as an AECO. It is accredited by the Bureau as an importer and as a Customs Facility Warehouse Operator, and accredited by the Civil Aeronautics Board as a freight forwarder. It is also a member of CAPEC, certified as an operator of a regional hub for express shipments, and has a dedicated air carrier and an integrated end-to-end tracking system. Which additional requirement must it still satisfy under Section 12?

choices.A: An IT System capable of interfacing with the Bureau's automated system
choices.B: Accreditation by the Bureau as a Customs Broker
choices.C: A security deposit of not less than Php5,000,000.00 maintained with an AAB
choices.D: A notarized written commitment from an AAB submitted to the District Collector

level2.reason: Sec. 12 requires an applicant to have: importer accreditation (12.1), Customs Facility Warehouse Operator accreditation (12.2), CAB accreditation as freight forwarder (12.3), proof of membership in an international organization such as CAPEC (12.4), certification as a global or regional hub operator (12.5), a dedicated air carrier (12.6), an integrated end-to-end tracking system (12.7), and an IT System capable of interfacing with the Bureau's automated system (12.8). Kestrel has items 12.1 to 12.7, so only 12.8 remains. Customs Broker accreditation is not listed, and the security deposit and notarized commitment relate to Low-Value releases rather than accreditation.

level2.question: An AECO's MAWB contains 40 HAWBs, all with FOB value below Php10,000.00, covered by a detailed e-CIFCM submitted before arrival. Two of the HAWBs cover Regulated Goods. How should the goods be declared under the CAO?

choices.A: The detailed e-CIFCM serves as the goods declaration for all 40 HAWBs, including the two covering Regulated Goods
choices.B: Each of the 40 HAWBs must be declared individually through the Customs Cargo Clearance System under formal entry
choices.C: The detailed e-CIFCM serves as the goods declaration for the other 38, while the Regulated Goods are declared separately per HAWB
choices.D: The other 38 need a simplified goods declaration, while the Regulated Goods are covered by the e-CIFCM

level2.reason: All 40 HAWBs are below Php10,000.00, so they are De Minimis Shipments. Under Sec. 6.2.1, the detailed e-CIFCM also serves as the goods declaration for De Minimis Shipments, but Regulated Goods shall be declared separately per HAWB. Therefore the e-CIFCM covers the 38 non-regulated HAWBs, and the two HAWBs with Regulated Goods are declared separately. Formal entry (Sec. 6.4) and the simplified goods declaration (Sec. 6.3.2) apply to other categories.

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang taon mula sa date ng final payment ng duties at taxes o Customs Clearance maaaring mag-conduct ang Bureau ng audit examination ng records, ayon sa Sec. 4.1.1?

choices.A: Isang (1) taon
choices.B: Tatlong (3) taon
choices.D: Sampung (10) taon

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 4.1.1 (at Sec. 5.3), sa loob ng tatlong (3) taon mula sa date ng final payment ng duties at taxes o Customs Clearance, maaaring mag-conduct ang Bureau ng audit examination, inspection, verification, at investigation ng records na may kaugnayan sa goods declaration.

level1.question: Ano ang Inadvertent Error ayon sa Sec. 3.6?

choices.A: Sinadyang paggamit ng maling tariff heading para bawasan ang duties at taxes
choices.B: Sinadyang maling declaration ng quantity o weight para umiwas sa regulasyon
choices.C: Kabiguang magtago ng records sa Principal Place of Business ng Importer
choices.D: Unintentional na mechanical, electronic, o clerical error ng Importer na katumbas ng simple Negligence

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 3.6, ang Inadvertent Error ay mechanical, electronic, o clerical error na hindi sinasadya ng Importer sa kabila ng pagpapanatili ng internal controls, at itinuturing na simple Negligence. Ang sinadyang pagkilos ay mas malapit sa Fraud (Sec. 3.3).

level1.question: Aling operating unit ng PCAG ang nagsasagawa ng audit examination, inspection, verification, o investigation ng records, ayon sa Sec. 5.3?

choices.A: PCAG-CAO
choices.B: PCAG-TIRAO
choices.D: DOF-FAIU

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 5.3, ang PCAG-Compliance Assessment Office (PCAG-CAO) ang gumagawa ng audit work plan at nagsasagawa ng audit examination, inspection, verification, o investigation ng records. Ang PCAG-TIRAO naman ay para sa trade data review, risk-based profiling, at pag-develop ng audit policies at procedures.

level1.question: Gaano katagal valid ang Audit Notification Letter (ANL) mula sa date ng issuance, ayon sa Sec. 5.5.1(b)?

choices.A: 15 calendar days
choices.B: 60 calendar days
choices.D: 90 calendar days

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 5.5.1(b), ang ANL ay valid sa loob ng thirty (30) calendar days mula sa date ng issuance, at maaaring i-revalidate ng Assistant Commissioner para sa isa pang thirty (30) days bago ito mag-expire.

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 6.1.2, gaano katagal ang ibinibigay sa Importer na nakatanggap na ng ANL para mag-avail pa rin ng PDP sa pamamagitan ng pagsumite ng application at pagbabayad ng deficiency?

choices.A: 30 calendar days mula sa receipt ng ANL
choices.B: 90 calendar days mula sa receipt ng ANL
choices.C: 60 calendar days mula sa receipt ng ANL
choices.D: 120 calendar days mula sa receipt ng ANL

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 6.1.2, ang Importer na nakatanggap ng ANL ay maaari pa ring mag-avail ng PDP kung magsusumite siya ng application at magbabayad ng deficiency duties, taxes, at penalties sa loob ng ninety (90) calendar days mula sa receipt ng ANL.

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 6.3.1, ano ang babayaran ng PDP applicant na hindi pa nakakatanggap ng ANL?

choices.A: Deficiency sa duties at taxes plus 10% penalty ng basic deficiency
choices.B: Deficiency sa duties at taxes plus 125% ng revenue loss
choices.C: Deficiency sa duties at taxes plus 20% surcharge sa dutiable value
choices.D: Deficiency sa duties at taxes plus legal interest

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 6.3.1, ang PDP applicant na hindi pa nakatatanggap ng ANL ay magbabayad ng deficiency sa duties at taxes plus legal interest ayon sa Sec. 7. Ang 10% penalty ay para sa applicant na nakatanggap na ng ANL (Sec. 6.3.2).

level1.question: Alin sa mga sumusunod na goods declarations ang hindi qualified sa PDP ayon sa Sec. 6.2?

choices.A: Goods declarations na may Inadvertent Error
choices.B: Goods declarations na may deficiency sa duties at taxes
choices.D: Goods declarations ng Importer na hindi pa nakatatanggap ng ANL

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 6.2.3, hindi qualified sa PDP ang goods declarations na may Fraud ayon sa Sec. 10.3.2. Hindi rin qualified ang mga goods declarations na subject ng pending cases sa ibang Customs office (Sec. 6.2.1) o sa courts (Sec. 6.2.2).

level1.question: Ayon sa Sec. 10.3.2, ano ang fine para sa Fraud na napatunayang ginawa?

choices.A: Six (6) times ng revenue loss
choices.B: 125% ng revenue loss
choices.D: 20% ng dutiable value ng goods

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 10.3.2, ang offender na guilty sa Fraud ay mapaparusahan ng fine na katumbas ng six (6) times ng revenue loss at/o imprisonment na hindi bababa sa dalawang (2) taon pero hindi lalampas sa walong (8) taon.

level1.question: Sa loob ng ilang araw mula sa receipt ng denial ng Commissioner sa request for reconsideration o reinvestigation maaaring mag-appeal ang Importer sa Court of Tax Appeals (CTA), ayon sa Sec. 8?

choices.A: 15 araw
choices.B: 60 araw
choices.D: 90 araw

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 8, kapag ang request for reconsideration o reinvestigation ay denied, buo man o bahagi, ng Commissioner, maaaring mag-appeal ang Importer sa CTA sa loob ng thirty (30) days mula sa receipt ng adverse ruling o decision.

level1.question: Ilang porsyento kada taon ang interest na ipinapataw sa deficiency duties, taxes, at other charges, ayon sa Sec. 7?

choices.A: 6% per annum
choices.B: 20% per annum
choices.D: 25% per annum

level1.reason: Sa Sec. 7, ang interest na twenty percent (20%) per annum, na binibilang mula sa date ng final assessment ayon sa Sec. 429 ng CMTA, ay ipinapataw sa PDP availment, deficiency duties, taxes at other charges, at fine o penalty, kung mayroon.

level2.question: A goods declaration for an importation by Seaview Imports Inc. was filed by its customs broker, Reyes Brokerage, on 10 March 2022. Seaview made its final payment of duties and taxes on 15 March 2022, and the Customs Clearance was granted on 20 March 2022. Assume three years is counted to the same calendar date. Until when must each keep the records of the transaction at its Principal Place of Business?

choices.A: Seaview until 15 March 2025; Reyes Brokerage until 10 March 2025
choices.B: Seaview until 20 March 2025; Reyes Brokerage until 20 March 2025
choices.C: Seaview until 20 March 2025; Reyes Brokerage until 10 March 2025
choices.D: Seaview until 10 March 2025; Reyes Brokerage until 15 March 2025

level2.reason: Under the first paragraph of Sec. 4.4, importers keep records for three years from the date of final payment of duties and taxes or Customs Clearance, whichever is later, which is 20 March 2022, so until 20 March 2025. Under the second paragraph, parties engaged in Customs Clearance and processing keep records for three years from the date of filing of the goods declaration, which is 10 March 2022, so until 10 March 2025.

level2.question: The PCAG served an Audit Notification Letter (ANL) on Northgate Corp. on 5 August 2024. Northgate did not manifest an intention to avail of the PDP. Assume days are counted starting the day after service. By what date must the audit team commence the audit proper?

choices.A: 4 September 2024
choices.B: 4 October 2024
choices.D: 3 December 2024

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.5.1(d), the audit team must commence the audit proper not later than sixty (60) calendar days from the service of the ANL, unless the importer manifests an intention to avail of the PDP. Sixty days counted from 5 August 2024 ends on 4 October 2024.

level2.question: Delta Foods Inc. received an ANL on 1 February 2025. The audit covers two years of importations. Assuming no extension, what is the period, counted from the date it received the ANL, within which the audit should be completed?

choices.A: 240 calendar days
choices.B: 120 calendar days
choices.D: 360 calendar days

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.5.1(d), the audit shall be completed within one hundred twenty (120) calendar days per year of audit period from the date the Importer receives the ANL. For a two-year audit period, the period is 2 x 120 = 240 calendar days.

level2.question: Orient Trading Corp. received a Demand Letter signed by the Commissioner on 10 June 2025. It wants to contest the deficiency assessment based on its existing records, without presenting additional evidence. Assume days are counted starting the day after receipt. What may it file, with whom, and by when?

choices.A: A request for reinvestigation with the PCAG by 10 July 2025
choices.B: A request for reconsideration with the Court of Tax Appeals by 25 June 2025
choices.C: A request for reconsideration with the Secretary of Finance by 25 June 2025
choices.D: A request for reconsideration with the Commissioner by 25 June 2025

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.5.1(f), the adversely affected Importer may file a request for reconsideration or reinvestigation with the Commissioner within fifteen (15) days from receipt of the Demand Letter, which ends on 25 June 2025. Under Secs. 3.14 and 3.15, reconsideration is based on existing records, while reinvestigation requires newly discovered or additional evidence.

level2.question: Harbor Metals Inc. filed a request for reinvestigation of audit findings on 1 July 2025 and submitted all relevant supporting documents on 20 July 2025. Assume days are counted starting the day after the triggering date. By what date must the PCAG resolve the request?

choices.A: 19 August 2025
choices.B: 18 September 2025
choices.D: 18 October 2025

level2.reason: Under Sec. 5.5.1(f), the Importer must submit all supporting documents within thirty (30) days from the date of filing, which Harbor Metals did on 20 July 2025. The PCAG then has sixty (60) calendar days from submission of the complete documents to resolve the request. Sixty days from 20 July 2025 ends on 18 September 2025.

level2.question: Pacific Sourcing Corp. received an ANL on 2 September 2025 and filed its PDP application on 1 October 2025, paying the deficiency. On 10 October 2025, it discovered a new issue that needs to be disclosed. Assume days are counted starting the day after the triggering date. What is the last day to amend the application and pay additional deficiency duties, taxes and penalties?

choices.A: 1 December 2025
choices.B: 30 November 2025
choices.D: 31 December 2025

level2.reason: Under Sec. 6.1.2, the Importer may amend the PDP application and pay additional deficiency duties, taxes and penalties within an additional non-extendible period of thirty (30) calendar days from the filing of the PDP application form. Thirty days from 1 October 2025 ends on 31 October 2025. The 90-day period from receipt of the ANL does not extend this amendment period.

level2.question: Greenfield Corp. received an ANL and then availed of the PDP under Sec. 6.1.2, and its application was approved. Its basic deficiency in duties and taxes is Php 500,000.00, and it made no disclosure on royalties. Ignoring legal interest, how much must it pay under the Order?
level2.reason: Under Sec. 6.3.2, a PDP applicant who has received an ANL and availed of the program under Sec. 6.1.2 pays the deficiency plus a penalty of ten percent (10%) of the basic deficiency, plus legal interest. The penalty is 10% x Php 500,000.00 = Php 50,000.00, so the payment is Php 550,000.00. Under Sec. 6.3, these replace the penalties in Sec. 10.3.1.

level2.question: Lakeside Importers Inc. learned that its seller received subsequent proceeds from the resale of the imported goods on 5 May 2025, and it has not received any ANL. It filed its PDP application and paid the deficiency of Php 200,000.00 only on 20 June 2025, which is 46 days after the proceeds accrued. What payment treatment applies under the Order?

choices.A: Deficiency only, without penalty and interest
choices.B: Deficiency plus legal interest
choices.C: Deficiency plus 10% penalty and legal interest
choices.D: Deficiency plus a fine of 125% of the revenue loss

level2.reason: Under Sec. 6.3.3, the no-penalty and no-interest treatment for disclosures on subsequent proceeds applies only if the applicant files within thirty (30) calendar days from the accrual of the proceeds. Lakeside acted after 46 days, so the disclosure falls under Sec. 6.3.1 or 6.3.2. Because it has not received an ANL, Sec. 6.3.1 applies: deficiency plus legal interest.

level2.question: During a post clearance audit, Metro Imports Corp. cannot produce any records for an importation with a dutiable value of Php 2,000,000.00. What surcharge may be imposed on it for failure to keep records under the Order?
level2.reason: Under Sec. 10.1.2, a surcharge of twenty percent (20%) on the dutiable value of the goods for which no records were kept and maintained is imposable for failure to keep records. 20% x Php 2,000,000.00 = Php 400,000.00.

level2.question: Bayan Trading Co. is a delinquent importer whose audit resulted in deficiency duties and taxes of Php 9,500.00, with Php 3,000.00 in interest and penalties, for a total of Php 12,500.00. Can the Bureau use distraint and levy to collect?

choices.A: No, because the duties and taxes alone are not more than Php 10,000.00
choices.B: Yes, because the total with interest and penalties exceeds Php 10,000.00
choices.C: Yes, because the Bureau may pursue any remedy at its discretion
choices.D: No, because distraint and levy apply only to real property

level2.reason: Under Sec. 9.3, distraint and levy are not allowed when the amount of duties and taxes, excluding interest and penalties, is not more than Php 10,000.00. Bayan's duties and taxes are Php 9,500.00, so the Bureau cannot use these remedies, even though the total with interest and penalties is Php 12,500.00.
